caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 663-64 of 2009
parties:
Siddiqur Rahman and others ------ Petitioners (in both cases)
Vs.
Nek Pervin Islam and others ------ Respondents (in both cases)
full_judgment:
3. Respondent No. 1, Nek Parvin Islam, as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 88 of 1992 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka (now Joint District Judge) for declaration of title in 2½ kathas of land described in schedule-'Ka' to the plaint (hereinafter referred to as the suit land) and for recovery of khas possession of the flat described in schedule-'Gha' to the plaint out of 3(three) storied building from added defendant Nos. 9-11 and for cancellation of kabala No. 11689 dated 24.09.1977 of Dhaka Sadar Sub-Registrar's Office as described in schedule-'Kha' to the plaint allegedly executed by her in favour of her father, A.K.M. Abdullah (since deceased) and her step mother, Begum Sufia Abdullah who were impleaded in the suit as defendant Nos. 1 and 3 respectively as void, illegal, collusive and inoperative. 

 4. The case of the plaintiff, in short, was that her father-AKM Abdullah purchased the suit land with his own money in the benami of her mother-Amena Khatoon, defendant No. 2 by two registered kabalas being Nos. 3660 and 3661 both dated 07.08.1967. The plaintiff was born on 01.01.1965 and the marriage of her mother with her father was dissolved mutually in 1971 and prior to that the suit land was orally gifted to her by her mother and the witnesses (names of the witnesses have been mentioned in the plaint) present at the time of making the gift took formal delivery of possession of the gifted land on her behalf; the said gift was confirmed by her mother swearing an affidavit before the Notary Public on 18.04.1971. The gift was made in presence of plaintiff’s father with his consent who is also an attesting witness in the affidavit confirming the gift. Subsequently, the plaintiffs father created a registered sale deed bearing No. 11689 dated 29.04.1977 showing transfer of the suit land along with another 2½ kathas of land belonging to one Jahanara Khatoon, defendant No. 4, i.e. in total 5(five) kathas of land, in his favour and in favour of her step mother-Sufia Khatun, defendant No. 3. The plaintiffs father got her signature in some stamp papers telling her that a power of attorney would be made for taking loan from the House Building Finance Corporation for making construction on the suit land. The construction on the suit land was made by taking loan from the House Building Finance Corporation; the plaintiff herself constructed the incomplete 3rd floor with her husband's money and she is living therein with her family members and her name has been duly mutated in the record of right. The plaintiff is also in possession of the northem part of the ground floor of the building. After attaining majority, the plaintiff requested her father to hand over the documents relating to her property, but on this plea and that plea, her father avoided the same. The plaintiff's mother- Amena Khatun filed Title Suit No. 420 of 1981 in the Third Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka which, on transfer to the Court of Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka, was renumbered as Title Suit No. 181 of 1992 for declaration of her title in respect of the suit land (earlier gifted to her) without impleading her in the said suit. The suit was dismissed on the finding, inter alia, that Amena Khatun was the benamder of AKM Abdullah (the plaintiffs father) in respect of the suit land. The plaintiff came to know that her father and her step mother executed and registered 3(three) sale deeds bearing Nos. 1245, 1246 and 1247 all dated 03.05.1992 showing transfer of 3¼ kathas of land (each deed showing transfer of 1¼ kathas of land) in favour of defendant Nos. 6-8 and delivered possession of 3(three) rooms of the second floor and 2(two) rooms of the northern portion of the ground floor to them through tenant-defendant Nos. 9-11 who are now in illegal possession thereof without having any valid, right, title and interest therein. The defendants denied the title of the plaintiff on 15.05.1992; hence she was compelled to file the suit for the aforementioned reliefs. 

 6. In the written statement of defendant 1 Nos. 6-8, it was contended, inter alia, that defendant No. 1, father of the plaintiff purchased the suit land in the benami of his wife-Amena Khatun, mother of the plaintiff by kabala dated 07.08.1967 and defendant No. 4-Jahanara Khatun purchased contiguous western 02½ kathas of land by two registered kabalas of the same date from the same vendor. Defendant No. 2-Amena Khatun, mother of the plaintiff, eloped from custody of defendant No. 1 to marry one Tajul Islam leaving her in the custody of defendant No. 1 who brought up the minor plaintiff and gave marriage with one Shafiqul Islam in 1976. Defendant No. 1 married defendant No. 3, Begum Sufia Abdullah. To avoid future threat to his title in the suit land from defendant No. 2, the plaintiff, was made the owner of the suit land showing a colourable transfer by way of oral gift by defendant No. 2 and on receipt of proper consideration, the plaintiff voluntarily agreed to make a sale deed in respect of the suit land in favour of her father and step mother and accordingly, she joined her name as one of the vendors along with defendant No. 4-Jahanara Begum and transferred the suit land along with contiguous western 2½ kathas of land by a common sale deed being No. 11689 dated 20.04.1977. After the said kabala, defendant Nos. 1 and 3 obtained a revised plan from the then Dhaka Improvement Trust (DIT) for construction of a building on 3¾ kathas of land out of said 5(five) kathas of land and when they proceeded for obtaining loan from defendant No. 5, House Building Finance Corporation, upon the objection raised by defendant No. 2, sanctioned loan was withheld. In the circumstances, defendant No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 156 of 1979 in the Third Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and got a decree in his favour. Then after getting loan of taka 1,76,000.00 from defendant No. 5, defendant No. 1 extended construction of the 1st floor and completed two units of the 1st floor and one unit of the 6. 2nd floor and possessed major portions of  the building through monthly tenants and allowed his daughter, the plaintiff to live in a room of the 2nd floor as a licensee and thus, while defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 3 were in possession of the building on 3¾ kathas of land, they in order to repay the loan amount sold vacant land measuring 4¼ kathas outside the building area to defendant Nos. 9 and 10 and one 1 Mohammad Yakub Ali by registered E kabala No. 4639 dated 23.12.1985 in which purchasers are in separate exclusive possession by opening separate holding number and thereafter, defendant Nos. 1 and 3 sold the remaining undivided 33/4 kathas of land and building to the defendants by three registered kabalas being Nos. 1245, 1246 and 1247 all dated 03.05.1992 and handed over possession of the land and building with the licensee, that is, the plaintiff to them. The defendants are the bonafide purchasers of the suit land for value without any notice of fraud committed by defendant Nos. 1 or 3 alleged by the plaintiff. The plaintiff saying no right, title and interest in the suit and being in possession in a portion of the suit land as a licensee was not entitled; to get any relief in the suit and the same was liable to be dismissed. 

 7. The petitioners who were defendant Nos. 6-8 in Title Suit No. 88 of 1992, filed a separate suit being Tide Suit No. 255 of 1993 in the Fourth Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka which on transfer to the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka was renumbered as Title Suit No. 28 of 1995 for declaration of title in 3¾ kathas of land and for eviction of Nek Parvin Islam, the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 88 of 1992 making the same averments as made in the written statement filed in Title Suit No. 88 of 1992. Nek Parvin Islam, plaintiff of Title Suit No. 88 of 1992 who was impleaded in Title Suit No. 25 of 1992 as defendant No. 1 filed written statement therein stating same facts as stated in the plaint of Title Suit No. 88 of 1992. 

 8. Defendant No. 2 in her written statement contended, inter alia, that the suit land was purchased in her own name by the money given by her parents by kabala dated 07.08.1967. After purchase, she developed the land by filling earth and after obtaining plan from the then DIT constructed building thereon by the money paid by her parents and brothers. The suit land was never purchased by defendant No. 1 in her benami and he never paid money for purchasing the same. The Plaintiff deposed in Title Suit No. 420 of 1991 supporting her. The plaintiff was born in 1959. As defendant No. 1 was not a man of good moral character, quarrel used to take place oft and often between herself and defendant No. 1 for which she was compelled to go for separation and subsequently married one Tajul Islam. The plaintiff was brought up in the suit land under the care of the defendant and was married to one Shafiqul Islam and they were living in the suit property as her caretaker and also as her licensee. The defendant never gifted the suit land to the plaintiff and there was no reason as well for such gift, had she any intention to transfer the suit land she would have done so by executing a registered deed. Defendant No. 1 having failed to grab the suit property of the defendant by adopting various tactics one after another, lastly created a fraudulent deed and obtained loan from defendant No. 5 illegally this was not binding upon her. The defendant had been exercising her right of possession in the suit land through her daughter and son-in-law. The plaintiff f by revising the plan of DIT constructed the first floor. The defendant never mortgaged the suit land with the House Building Finance Corporation. The plaintiff inducted one Kabirul Islam as a tenant of defendant No. 2 and he paid rents to the plaintiff as a tenant of the defendant. The sale deed dated 20.04.1977 being deed No. 11689 from the plaintiff was illegal, void and without any effect and the same was liable to be declared void and by the said kabala, defendant No. 1 did not acquire any right and title in the suit land. 

 9. Both suits were heard analogously and the learned Subordinate Judge by his judgment and decree dated 15.11.2000 (two separate decrees were drawn up and signed) dismissed Title Suit No. 88 of 1992 and decreed Title Suit No. 28 of 1995. 

 10. Value of Title Suit No. 28 of 1995 being taka 60,000.00 only, defendant No. 1 (Nek Parvin Islam) filed appeal: before the District Judge, Dhaka being Title Appeal No. 767 of 2000 against the judgment and decree passed therein. Nek Parvin Islam being the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 88 of 1992 filed Appeal from Original Decree No. 158 of 2001 before the High Court Division against the judgment and decree passed therein Subsequently, Title Appeal No. 767 of 2000 was transferred to the High Court Division from the Court of the District; Judge, Dhaka and was renumbered as Transfer Appeal No. 648 of 2001. A Division Bench of the High Court 1 Division after hearing the appeal from original decree and the transfer appeal analogously by the impugned judgment and decree allowed both appeals in part in the following terms: 

 "Accordingly the First Appeal No. 158 of 2001 and the Transfer Appeal No. 648 of 2001 are allowed in part with cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 15.11.2000 passed in T.S. No. 88/92 and T.S. No. 28/95 are set aside and both T.S. No. 88/92 and T.S. No. 28/95 are decreed in part. The right, title and interest of Nek Parvin Islam, plaintiff in Title Suit No. 88 of 1992 and defendant No. 1(sic) Title Suit No. 28 of 1995, in respect of 2½ kathas of land corresponding to 0.0410 acres of land out of 0.0825 acres in plot No. 117(old plot No. 41/42) acquired through gift made by Amena Khatoon "in presence and with consent" of A.K.M. Ahdullah is declared to be Valid and the alleged sale of said 2½ kathas of land belonged to Nek Parvin Islam vide registered sale deed No. 3660 dated 27.4.67 and registered sale deed No. 3661 dated 7.8.67 P.S. Ramna Sadar Sub-Registrar, Dhaka each for 1¼ kathas, vide Sale Deed No. 11689 dated 29.4.77 as well as vide Sale Deed No. 1245, 1246 and 1247 all dated 3.5.92 is declared to be illegal and void. The said Nek Parvin Islam however will have no right and title on the building constructed on the said 3¾ kathas of land but shall have possessory right because of her ownership on 2½ kathas of land. Messrs Siddiqur Rahman, Md. Sirajul Islam and Farida Yeasmin do have joint possession on the building constructed on the said 3¾ kathas of land with ownership only on the balance 1¼ kathas of land with joint possession. The respective shares in the joint possession may be determined mutually or through a proper suit in accordance with law and till then the said Nek Parvin Islam, Siddiqur Rahman Md. Sirajul Islam and Mrs. Farida Yeasmin shall continue to possess and enjoy the suit property jointly." 

 11. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division in Appeal from Original Decree No. 158 of 2001 and Transfer Appeal No. 648 of 2001 defendant Nos. 6-8 have filed Civil Petitions for Leave Appeal Nos. 663 of 2009 and 664 of 2009 respectively before this Division. 

 12. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Counsel, appearing for the leave petitioners in both leave petitions, has submitted that the High Court Division committed grave error of law in allowing the appeals in part declaring the right, title and interest of Nek Parvin Islam (the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 88 of 1992) in respect of 2½ kathas of land (the suit land) on the basis of alleged oral gift made by defendant No. 2 of the suit and the sale deed dated 29.04.1977 being deed No. 11689 so far as , it relates to 2½ kathas of land, that is, the suit land and the sale deed Nos. 1245, 1246 1 and 1247 all dated 03.05.1992 executed by defendant Nos. 1 and 3 in favour of defendant Nos. 6-8 as illegal and void inasmuch as it did not reverse the finding of the trial Court that the plaintiff failed to prove her case of acquisition of title in the suit land on the basis of oral gift by her mother, defendant No. 2, who was a benamder of defendant No. 1 only; defendant No. 2 being the benamder of defendant No. 1 she was not legally entitled to make the alleged gift in favour of the defendant. He has further submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in declaring the deed dated 29.04.1977 void inasmuch as the plaintiff failed to prove the allegation of fraud in executing and registering the deed by her particularly when she did not deny the fact of execution of the same. He has further submitted that the High Court Division failed to consider the admitted fact that it is the plaintiffs father who constructed the building on the suit land along with other land by obtaining loan from the House Building Finance Corporation and the plaintiff is in possession in a portion thereof as a licensee of her father in their proper perspective and thus, erred in law in decreeing the suit in part. He has further submitted that the finding of the learned Judges of the High Court Division as to the minority of the plaintiff at the time of execution and registration of the kabala dated 29.04.1977 accepting her date of birth as 01.01.1965 is not based on proper appreciation of the evidence on record particularly in the face of the evidence DW4, the mother of the plaintiff and thus fell into an error in holding that the said kabala transferring the suit land as void being hit by section 11 of the Contract Act and also the deeds of defendant Nos. 6-8 executed by defendant Nos. 1 and 3 as void. 

 14. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, learned Counsel, entering caveat on behalf of respondent No. 1 in both leave petitions, on the other hand, has supported the impugned judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division by submitting that the learned Judges approached the case from correct stand point and correctly sifted the evidence on record in holding that at the time of execution and registration of the kabala dated 29.04.1977, the plaintiff being minor, the same was void within the meaning of section 11 of the Contract Act and that the plaintiff acquired title to the suit land on the basis of the oral gift made by her mother, the ostensible owner in presence and with the consent of defendant No. 1, her father, the real owner. 

 15. From the impugned judgment and decree, it appears that the High Court Division formulated two points for its decision (i) whether the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 88 of 1992, who is defendant No. 1 in Title Suit No. 28 of 1995, is the real owner of the suit land measuring 21/2 kathas of land gifted by her mother with the consent of her father as described in schedule-'Ka' to the plaint and is in possession therein with others; (ii) whether the sale deed bearing No. 1168 dated 29.04.1977 showing Nek Parvin Islam and Jahanara Begum as the vendors in favour of AKM Abdullah and Begum Sufia Abdullah as the purchasers is valid, so far as it relates to the sale by Nek Parvin Islam in respect of 2½ kathas of land, she being minor at the relevant time. 

 17. Admittedly, the suit land measuring an area of 2½ kathas was purchased by plaintiffs (Nek Parvin Islam) father in the benami of her mother-Amena Khatun (since divorced) by kabala dated 07.08.1967. The case of the plaintiff is that while she was minor her mother being the ostensible owner of the suit land gifted the same to her in presence of her father, defendant No. 1 and with his consent and the gift was accepted on her behalf by the witnesses present at the time of making the gift; subsequently, defendant No. 2 in support of the oral gift had sworn an affidavit before a notary public on 18.04.1977 wherein her father figured as an attesting witness. The High Court Division believed the case of the plaintiff of acquisition of title by her to the suit land on the basis of the oral gift made by her mother, the ostensible owner and also found her possession in the suit land on the basis of her own title. In coming to the said findings, the High Court Division considered 4(four) facts (a) Amena Khatun, the plaintiffs mother was the ostensible owner (b) the oral gift was made by defendant No. 2 in favour of Nek Parvin Islam with the consent of the real owner, defendant No. 1 and in his presence (c) defendant No. 1 became an attesting witness in the affidavit sworn by Amena Khatun in support of oral gift made in favour of Nek Parvin Islam and (d) in the Kabala dated 29.04.1977 allegedly executed and registered by Nek Parvin Islam, defendant No. 1, the real owner, admitted the said fact of oral gift by defendant No. 2 in favour of the plaintiff and accepting her as the owner of the suit land purchased the same from her. We find nothing wrong with the High Court' Division in taking into account the said facts in finding title of the plaintiff, Nek Parvin Islam in the suit land on the basis of oral gift by Amena Khatun. Because at the time of oral gift admittedly defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 2 were the husband and the wife respectively and defendant No. 1, the real owner by those open overt acts gave up his right, title and interest in the suit land. In this regard, we like to put emphasis on the legal phraseology that 'one cannot approbate and reprobate.' It further appears that the plaintiff as PW1 deposed in support of her case of acquisition of title in the suit land on the basis of oral gift by Amena Khatun. PW2 Monir Hossain, a man of aged about 70 years clearly corroborated the plaintiff’s case of oral gift by her mother, defendant No. 2 by deposing that he was present at the time of making the gift. Although during pendency of the suit, plaintiffs father, AKM Abdullah died, the fact that he became an attesting witness in the affidavit sworn by Amena Khatun confirming the oral gift made by her in favour of her daughter, Nek Parvin Islam, in respect of the suit land was not denied by his legal heir, defendant No. 1(a) and defendant No. 3. Further, there being clear recitals in the kabala dated 29.04.1977 as to the fact of transfer of the suit land in favour of plaintiff, Nek Parvin Islam by way of oral gift by defendant No. 2, the High Court Division rightly found that the plaintiff, Nek Parvin Islam acquired title therein on the basis of oral gift made by defendant No. 2. But the trial Court did not consider these facts in giving finding that the plaintiff failed to prove her case of oral gift by defendant No. 2 in respect of the suit land and thus fell into an error in dismissing the suit of Nek Parvin Islam. 

 18. The High Court Division in holding that at the time of alleged execution and registration of the kabala dated 29.04.1977 by the plaintiff, she was minor accepted the case of the plaintiff that she was born on 01.01.1965. In accepting the plaintiffs date of birth as on 01.01.1965 the High Court Division relied upon the birth certificate issued by the Headmistress of Siddheswari Girls High School and her testimony as PW3 (when. she deposed, she retired as the Headmistress of the School). PW3, Rahima Khatun deposed that in the School admission Register, the date of birth of the plaintiff was recorded as 01.01.1965 and she proved the birth certificate issued by her as exhibit-1(Ka). The High Court Division also relied upon an affidavit sworn by the plaintiffs mother-Amena Khatun on 02.07.1991 (exhibit-1) to the effect that she was born on 01.01.1965. Monir Hossain, PW2 aged about 70 years specifically stated in his cross-examination that in 1971 the age of Nek Parvin Islam was around 6/7 years and this clearly corroborated the birth certificate exhibit-1(Ka) and the declaration made by Amena Khatun on 02.07.1991 that the plaintiff was born on 01.01.1965. Whereas, the trial Court simply relied upon the deposition of DW4, (Amena Khatoon) mother of the plaintiff who deposed that Nek Parvin Islam was born in 1959 without considering that Monir Hossain (PW2) and Rahima Khatun (PW3) were independent witnesses and they had no reason to be partisan for the plaintiff. The trial Court also failed to consider that after Amena Khatun (DW 4) married one Tajul Islam, she filed Title Suit No. 420 of 1981 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Third Court, Dhaka (on being transferred to the Court of Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka the suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 181 of 1992) against defendant No. 1, AKM Abdullah for declaration of her title in the suit without impleading the plaintiff. Therefore, defendant No. 2 having set up her own title to the suit land in denial of plaintiffs title became a partisan and interested person, her evidence could not be accepted on the question of the date of birth of the plaintiff particularly when her testimony clearly contradicted the affidavits sworn by her, one giving declaration that she gifted the suit land to the plaintiff (exhibit-3) and the other declaring   the plaintiffs date of birth as 01.01.1965 (exhibit-1) and other evidence which belied the testimony of DW4 as discussed hereinbefore. The trial Court also failed to consider that the date of birth of plaintiff, Nek Parvin Islam as recorded in the admission register of the School was given when no dispute as to the right to the suit land arose, so that would get preference over the assertion of the contesting party, defendant No. 2. 

 22. It being a fact that after purchase of 5(five) kathas of land by kabala dated 29.04.1977 (2½ kathas from the plaintiff and 2½ kathas from Jahanara Khatoon) the plaintiffs father made construction on the 3¾ kathas of land which included 2½ kathas of land of the plaintiff by  taking loan from the House Building Finance Corporation, the High Court Division rightly declared plaintiff, Nek Parvin Islam's right, title and interest in respect of 2½ kathas of land (the sui land), but she will have no right and title on the building constructer thereon except "possessory right because of her owner ship on 2½ kathas of land." The High Court Division also rightly protected the possession of the contesting defendants by observing that they "do have joint possession on the building constructed on the said 3¾ kathas of land with ownership V only on the balance 1¼ kathas of land with joint possession." We fully endorse the observations of the High Court Division that "The respective shares in the joint possession may be determined mute ally or through a proper suit in accordance with law and till then the said Nek Parvin Islam, Siddiqur Rahman, Md. Sirajul Islam and Mrs. Farida yeasmin shall continue to possess and enjoy the suit property jointly." And we further observe that if any sui for partition is filed as observed by the, High Court Division, the trial Court would consider the case of the contesting defendants that they purchased 3¾ kathas of land along with the 3(three) storied building, standing thereon, but in no case, they shall have any claim over the suit land that is, 2½ kathas of land as described in scheduled-Ka to the plaint.

parties:
Akram Ali Pk. (MD) and others ----- Petitioner
Vs
Yasin Ali (Md) and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The facts, leading to the filing of this petition, in brief, are that the petitioners and others instituted Other Suit No. 300 of 2000 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, First Court, Bogra for declaration of their easement right to the suit ponds. Their case, in short, is that during the CS operation the suit ponds were recorded in the name of Bharat Samrat and the names of Gyanoda Prashad Sukul, Chandra Prashad Sukul and Jogodeshwari Debba were recorded as the possessors who had been enjoying the possession thereof on payment of rent to the concerned authority. After the death of those persons, the petitioners perform a respondents and the villagers of the respective villages had been enjoying the possession of the suit ponds claiming their easement right. The suit pond measuring 1.93 acres appertaining to CS Khatian No.17 containing Plot No. 709 belonged to one Jogodeshwari and others. In the remark's column of the said khatian that pond had been shown as being used 'by the public' but in the DP Khatian No.1362 the said pond had been wrongly recorded in the name of respondent No.2 having no right, title, interest and possession therein. The suit pond measuring 1.71 acres of plot No. 680 appertaining to CS khatian No. 17 is being used by the public but in the DP Khatian No. 538 the same had been wrongly recorded in the name of respondent No. 1. The suit pond measuring 0.23 acre of CS Khatian No. 17 containing plot No. 1108 belonged to Jogodeshwari and others and the said pond is also being used by the public but in DP Khatian No.1076 the same had been wrongly recorded in the name of respondent Nos. 3-5. It has further been alleged that the defendants-respondents in connivance with the settlement officials have managed to get their names recorded in DP Khatian in respect of the suit ponds. In fact, the petitioners and the general public have been enjoying the possession of the said ponds in exercise of their easement right. The cause of action of the suit arose on 15-11-2000 when the defendants-respondents obstructed the petitioners from exercising their right of easement in the suit ponds. Hence the suit. 

 4. On 16-5-2006, the petitioners filed an application under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the learned Senior Assistant Judge, First Court, Bogra for amendment of the plaint. They stated, inter alia, that owing to inadvertence some important facts have not been incorporated in the plaint. Not only correction of the description of the names of some of the plaintiffs is necessary but striking out the name of plaintiff No. 61 is also essential. Inclusion of CS Khatian No.18 containing plot Nos.709, 680 and 1108 essential and a paragraph to the effect that the plaintiffs-petitioners shall conduct the suit in representative character for declaration of their easement and customary right on replacing the original prayer for declaration of their title over the suit ponds is also necessary. 

 14. The plaintiffs instituted Other Class Suit No. 300 of 2000 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, First Court, Bogra, for declaration of title and for establishment of their easement right over the suit ponds. From the impugned judgment, it appears that the plaintiffs amended the plaint more than once. On 15-6-2006, the plaintiffs filed an application under Order VI, rule 17 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of plaint incorporating new facts and prayer. 

 "There is one limitation in amending a plaint which is well recognized, that is, the nature and character of a suit cannot be changed by amendment. It is not, however, always correctly appreciated as to what is meant by a change in the nature and character of the suit. For example, as in the present case, a simple suit for declaration of title to the suit land was converted following an alleged dispossession in the meantime, into a suit for recovery of possession by amendment. Can it be said that by adding a new prayer for recovery of possession there has been a change, although apparently it may seem so, in the nature and character of the suit? 'The answer is obviously no. Has there been a change in the nature and character of the suit then by adding the prayer for partition which was allowed by the learned Subordinate Judge? The answer again must be no, because the principle is that the nature and character of a suit do not change so long as the fundamental character of the suit remains the same." 

 22. In the above case, this Division has found that a suit for simple declaration of title to the suit land may continue with an additional prayer for recovery if the dispossession was made during pendency of the suit. Even in a suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession, the plaintiff may ask for partition and such amendment by introducing a relief for partition will not change the nature and character of the suit. 

 23. In the case of Managing Committee NMC Model High School vs Obaidur Rahman Chowdhury 31 DLR (AD) 133, the plaintiff initially filed a suit for permanent injunction. During progress of the suit the defendants raised some structures and then the plaintiff filed an application under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for amendment of plaint by adding a new prayer for declaration of title and recovery of possession of a portion alleged to have been encroached upon by the defendants. The plaintiffs paid advalorem court fee on the proposed amended plaint. The order of amendment was upheld by the Courts below. Turning down the contention of the defendants who stated that the proposed amendment would change the nature and character of the suit land this Division held as under:—
case_type_name: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal

parties:
Tarik Hossain and others……….Appellants
Vs.
Dulari Begum & others……..Respondents
full_judgment:
Nazrul Islam Chowdhury J: This appeal at the instance of the defendants as appellants has been brought challenging the judgment and decree dated 17-7-2001 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, Additional Court and Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 155 of 2001. 

 3. For the purpose of appreciation of the facts involved in this appeal it needs a brief narration thereof and these are, the instant suit being Title Suit No. 92 of 2000 was instituted before the Sub-ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka, seeking a decree for declaration that the judgment and decree on compromise passed in Title Suit No. 168 of 1991 dated 3-5-95 is illegal, void and fraudulent which is not binding upon the plaintiffs. 

 4. The suit was instituted by two ladies who are the daughters of late Abul Hasnat alias Badsha Miah by his second wife, defendant Nos. 1-4 are the sons and daughters of said Badsha Miah by 1st wife Shamsun Nahar while the defendant No.6 is the son of Badsha Miah by his 2nd wife Rezia Begum defendant No.5; Said Abul Hasnat Mohammad Hossain alias Badsha Miah had two wives, the 1st wife was late Samsun Nahar and the 2nd wife is Rezia Begum, defendant No.5 is the mother of the plaintiffs while defendant No.6 is the other brother through their mother Rezia; said Badsha Miah died on 24-4-91 leaving behind the plaintiffs and the defendants as his legal heirs' he has also left behind properties described in Schedule Ka, Kha, Ga and Gha of the plaint which includes land, building shop etc the property left behind by said Badsha Miah described in schedule Ka, Ga and Gha of the plaint has been in possession of the defendant Nos. 1-4; defendant No.5 Rezia Begum along with her minor children i.e. Dulari, Rena Akhter and Rana Talukder as plaintiffs instituted said Title Suit No. 168 of 1991 seeking partition of their share in the suit schedule land i.e. Ka, Kha, Ga and Gha of the plaint impleading the defendant Nos. 1-4 and their mother Samsun Nahar as defendants. 

 5. During pendency of the suit Shamsun Nahar died leaving behind the defendant Nos. 1-4 as her legal heirs in the said suit; it was also stated in the plaint that late Badsha Miah left behind properties worth Taka 3 crores as per calculation made in the year 1991 and during pendency of the said suit the plaintiff No.1 of Title Suit No. 168 of 1991 having been unduly influenced by the defendant No. 1 of that suit entered into a compromise to the detriment of the interest of her minor children namely plaintiff Nos. 2-4 without taking any guardianship certificate of her minor children under the Guardian and Words Act. At the time of alleged compromise the defendant Nos. 2-4 of Title Suit No. 168 of 1991 were minors despite such a position the defendant No.5 of this suit entered into a compromise with the defendant No. 1 ignoring the interest of her minor children putting her signatures in the compromise petition on behalf of her minor son and daughters; consequently a compromise decree was obtained practicing fraud upon the court on 3-5-1995 in Title Suit No. 168 of 1991. The plaintiffs having obtained majority, came to know about the said fraudulent decree and upon obtaining a certified copy thereof on 10-4-2000, instituted the instant suit being Title suit No. 92 of 2000, seeking the decree as aforesaid. 

 6. The defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 4 entered appearance upon filling a written statement stating inter alia that the suit is barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act as also it is barred by limitation. In the written statement answering defendants admits that Samsun Nahar was the 1st wife of Badsha Miah who died recently leaving behind the defendant No. 1 as only son and 3 daughters Asma Akhter, Kalpona Yesmin and Sanjeda Yesmin as her three daughters. Subsequently, Badsha Miah married Rezia Begum for the second time out of whom he left behind one son Rana Talukder and two daughters. It is admitted in the said written statement that Badsha Miah died leaving his children out of his two wives late Samsun Nahar and Rezia Begum. It is also stated in the written statement that Razia begum along with her children brought Title Suit No. 168 of 1991 for partition of their share in the land left behind by Badsha Miah and during pendency of that suit a compromise was effected in between the parties and Rezia Begum the plaintiff No. 1 of that suit put the signature on behalf of his three minor children i.e. defendant Nos. 2-4 upon obtaining permission from the court and in that compromise petition the plaintiffs ultimately relinquished their claim in favour of the defendants of Title Suit No. 168 of 1991 in respect of schedule Ka, Ga and Gha of the suit land; in that suit the plaintiffs got themselves satisfied upon taking schedule Kha land in their favour which is a property of 2 Khata with tin shed structures, therefore, defendants prayed for dismissal of the suit. It is also disclosed in the written statement that the defendant No. 5 using names of her two daughters brought the instant suit for illegal gain. 

 7. Having taken up the suit for hearing the learned Joint District Judge framed 6 (six) issues including one as to whether the decree in Title Suit No. 168 of 1991 is/was illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs in course of trial of the suit the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 examined themselves as witness Nos. 1 and 2 for the plaintiffs respectively while the defendant No. 1 as witness No. 1 for the defendants while one Mahbubur Rahman was examined as witness No. 2. Upon hearing, the trial court having considered the evidence and materials on record decreed the suit by his impugned judgment and decree dated 17-7-2001 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge Additional Court and Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka. As against the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 17-7-2001 the defendant No. 1 as appellant preferred the instant appeal. During pendency of the appeal when the matter was brought in the list for hearing at that stage an application for compromise was filed apparently on behalf of both the parties represented by Mr N K Saha, Advocate on behalf of the appellants and Mr MinaI Hossain, Advocate appearing for the respondents. The said application was filed sometimes in the early part of January 2012 before this Bench. On 26-1-2012 the application for compromise was taken up for hearing at one stage when the mother of the two respondents was present before the court, as such, a query was made by this court, as to why her two daughters have entered in to a compromise with such a shockingly meager amount of 12 (twelve) lakhs as against a vast property left behind by her late husband Badsha Miah which is worth crores, with a view to ascertain the genuineness of the compromise, therefore, we found it proper to put some questions to Rezia Begum since her two daughters were not present before this court. The lady having appeared before the court burst into tears and replied স্যার আমি অসহায় মহিলা এবং মেয়েরাও তাই। আমাদের পক্ষে আল্লাহ্ ছাড়া কেহ নাই। আমরা নিরুপায়।” The reply given by the lady to the court attracted serious attention of both the Bar and Bench since more than dozen lawyers both seniors and juniors were present before the court at that time. Leaving no scope for anyone present to accept that the compromise as a genuine one rather the situation unmistakably manifested that the com promise placed before this court was obtained by duress upon exerting undue influence upon the respondents but having left with no power of resistance to such aggression upon their legitimate right of inheritance over the property left behind by their admitted father, according to Muslim Family Law of Inheritance. 

 26. Turning back to the facts involved in this case we have already noticed that the 2nd wife along with her children initially brought a suit for partition and for allotment of their share in the property left behind by Badsha Miah but that suit was rendered infructuous by desperate attempt made by the eldest son through the I st wife namely, defendant No. 1 Tarique Hossain in that suit and it is he who had compelled the 2nd wife to go for a compromise for and on behalf of her minor children without any sanction under the Guardian and Words Act, namely the defendant No. 1 managed a decree on compromise for them in Title Suit No. 168 of 1991. This position was detected by the minor children of Razia after attainment their majority so they have legitimately brought the second suit namely the present one before us being Title Suit No. 92 of 2000 renumbered as Title Suit No. 155 of 2001 for set- ting-aside the fraudulent decree obtained in the earlier suit namely Title Suit No. 168 of 1991. The suit was contested, evidence was recorded both oral and documentary and on consideration of the evidence and materials on record the learned Joint District Judge decreed the suit setting-aside the previous fraudulent decree obtained in Title Suit No. 168 of 1991 and the said judgment and decree dated 17-7-2001 passed in Title Suit No. 155 of 2001 (re-numbered) by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, Additional Court and Artha Rin Adalat No.2 is in challenge before in the instant FA No. 527 of 2007. In the suit plaintiff No. 1 Dulari Begum was examined as PW 1 while the plaintiff No. 2 Rena was plaintiff witness No.2. 

 28. This witness also produced the documents. This witness also disclosed that the decree on compromise obtained in Title Suit No. 168 of 1991, at stage when both the plaintiffs were minors and after attaining majority they have heard about the existence of a fraudulent decree and upon obtained certified copy thereof they brought the suit. The plaint of Title Suit No. 168 of 1991, the judgment of the said suit and so-called compromise petition namely the solenama filed in that suit were produced in court which had been marked as Exhibits 1, 2 series. 

 30. Similar is the case of deposition of PW 2 Rina Akter who has amply corroborated her sister PW 1 Dulari Begum and on a perusal of the cross- examination portion of this witness we do not find anything to discard the testimony made by PW 2 in her deposition in chief although this witness made allegation has her mother defendant No.5 entered into an unholy alliance with the defendant No.1 in obtaining a fraudulent decree in Title Suit No. 168 of 1991. But the facts revealed before us in the instant suit and from the very statement made by Rezia before this court we find that nothing was done by Rezia rather taking advantages of her helplessness, it is the defendant No.1 who obtained a compromise decree upon exerting undue influence on her. 

 31. Defendant No.1 Tarique Hossain figured as DW 1 on a perusal of his deposition we find that he has admitted that his father got married twice and his mother Shamsun Nahar was his first wife and he along with his three sisters, who are defendant Nos. 2-4 were born out of the wedlock. This witness also admitted that his father also left behind his 2nd wife Razia Begum the defendant No.5 and one son and two daughters out of their wedlock and they are the defendant No.6 Rana Talukders and the two plaintiffs Dulari Begum and Rina, Akter and his father Badsha died on 24-1-191 leaving behind his children out of his two wives along with his said two wives as his legal heirs. This witness also produced the solenama and the decree in Title Suit No. 168 of 1991 (marked as Exhibit. Ka series) He also admitted that by the said solenama the plaintiffs of Title Suit. No. 168 of 1991 got a land of two khatas with a single storied structure over it situated at SA plot No. 1768 while the remaining properties left behind by Badsha Miah fell in the share of defendants of Title Suit No. 168 of 1991. This witness also produced Exhibit Kha. He also produced a sale deed baring No. 6280 dated 7-12-98 executed by Rezia in favour of one Habibur Rahman marked as Exhibit Gha. He also produced the order sheet of the earlier suit being partition suit No. 168 of 1991 marked Ga and the final decree made in that suit marked as Exhibit Gha. 

 32. Md Mahbubur Rahman, figured as DW 2 in the suit who deposed that his brother Habibur Rahman purchased two khatas of land fell in the share of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 164 of 1991 by a registered kabala dated 7-12-98. 

 34. We have carefully scrutinized the impugned judgment delivered by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.2 in Title Suit No. 155 of 2001 through Mr Abdus Salam Mondal and Mr Minai Hossain. Since we have asked Mr Abdus Salam Mondal who is the Deputy Attorney-General of this court to make his submission in favour of the appellants, if any found by him, with a view to safeguard the interest of the appellants since their advocate is not appearing before us and since the learned Advocate for the appellants though appeared initially and made this case heard in part but did not appear subsequently, therefore, we also felt obliged to take special care of the interest of the appellants but unfortunately we find nothing in their favour. Since the broad facts namely, two plaintiffs before us were admittedly minors at the time when previous decree; was obtained in Title Suit No. 168 of 1991, besides, the defendant No.6 was also a minor because he is the youngest child of Rezia Begum. We have also noticed that at the time of institution of the present suit namely Title Suit No. 92 of 2000 re-numbered as Title Suit No. 155 of 2001. This defendant No. 6 was also a minor of course he has obtained majority inthe meantime. We have also noticed that the compromise petition was signed by Rezia Begum on her own behalf as also on behalf of her minor children she put her signature without obtaining any certificate under the Guardian and Words Act. These two broad facts in our opinion, are good enough to brush aside the judgment and decree obtained in Title Suit No. 168 of 1991 through an alleged compromise, therefore, we find that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, now Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka did not commit any illegality in passing the impugned judgment and decree dated 17-7-2001 in Title Suit No.155 of 2001, (numbered) warranting interference by this court, rather it is evident that the findings arrived at by, the learned Sub-ordinate Judge in passing the impugned decree are based on proper consideration of the evidence and materials on record, with cogent reasons, Therefore; we do not find any substance in the appeal. 

 35. Accordingly, this appeal is hereby dismissed without any order as to costs. The judgment and decree passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge; Additional Court, and Artha Rin  Adalat No. 2, Dhakain Title SuitNo. 92 of2000 renumbered as 155 of2001 dated 17-7-2001 are here by up held. 

 36. In view of the judgment and order as above, in order to do justice to the down trodden children left by Badsha Miah through his 2nd wife Rezia we direct the learned District Judge, Dhaka to restore Title Suit No. 168 of 1991 to its original file and number even upon reconstruction of the records, if necessary since the decree passed in that suit has been set-aside, in the meantime, declaring that the same is not binding upon the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 92 of 2000 renumbered as Title Suit No. 155 of 2001 and upon revival of Title Suit No. 168 of 1991 the learned District Judge is also directed to transfer the same to any competent court for disposal starting from the. stage before, filing of the so-called compromise petition in that suit with a further direction to the trial court to take note of the findings and observations made by this .court ill, this judgment delivered by us in this First Appeal and to dispose of the partition suit in preliminary form within 6 (six) months, from the date of transfer there of to him by the learned District Judge as directed above and after passing the preliminary decree the court concerned should also be directed to proceed for a final decree within a reasonable time not beyond one year from the passing of the preliminary decree. 

 37. The learned District Judge is also directed to attach the property left by Badsha Miah described in the schedule Ka, Ga, Gha of the plaint of Title Suit No. 168 of 1991 appointing Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and the collector as receiver thereof for the purpose of protecting and preserving the property and its income derived from the attached property with a view to distribute the same amongst the heirs of Badsha Miah after ascertainment of their respective shares on the final disposal of the partition suit. The receiver be also directed to maintain possession of the part of the property where the parties are holding for their respective dwelling purposes but the remaining properties which are being held by tenants or for business purpose shall be brought under the control and management of the Receiver. The Deputy Commissioner and collector of Dhaka shall however be at liberty to engage any other suitable person for carrying out the directions of this court but the ultimate responsibility shall lie with the collector and the Deputy commissioner, Dhaka. 

 39. The receiver shall take over possession of the entire property descried in the schedule of the plaint of title suit (partition) No. 168 of 1991 then pending before sub-ordinate judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.2 Dhaka (disposed of on 3-5-95)-except the ones held by the plaintiffs and defendants for their respective dwelling purposes. The Receiver shall also maintain proper accounts of the income and furnish the same on each month before the trial Court.

 Vs

full_judgment:
The opposite Party No. 1, Shakhina as pre-emptor filed Miscellaneous (Pre-emption Case No. 17 of 1996 in the Court of 4th Assistant Judge, Gazipur Sadar, Gazipur seeking pre-emption of the case land under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 against the Opposite Party No. 1, Abdul Hakim Talukder as pre-emptee purchaser and opposite party No. 2, Monwara Begum as the vendor on the allegation that opposite party No. 2, Monwara Begum sold the case land to opposite party No. 1, Abdul Hakim by a kabala which was executed on 18-6-1996 and with a view to defeat the right of pre-emption the opposite party Nos. 1-2 collusively and cunningly described the deed of transfer as deed of exchange. The pre-emptor and opposite party No. 2, Monwara Begum both are co-sharer of the case holding by inheritance and no notice of transfer was served on her, the opposite party No. 1, Abdul Hakim is a stranger purchaser and hence the pre-emptor is legally entitled to preempt the transfer in question. The opposite party No. 2 as pre-emptee opposite party contested the case by filing a written objection contending that the case is not maintainable in law. The learned Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Gazipur Sadar after conclusion of trial by its judgment and Order dated 20-4-1994 rejected the said pre-emption case. 

 5. The present petitioner's case in short is that the petitioner having acquired the schedule property by a deed of exchange being No. 2042 dated 25-3-1999, mutated his name and has been enjoying the said land by erecting a two-storied building thereon. The petitioner was not aware about the pre-emption case as well as the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 1998; that on 29-5-2002 from a notice of Mouchak Police Sub-station, Kaliakoir, the petitioner for the 1st time came to know that the opposite party No. 1 herein as pre-emptor obtained an Pre-emption Order in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 1998 against the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioner namely, Md. Abdul Hakim Talukder, herein opposite party No. 2 The said pre-emption Order dated 30-8-2001 passed in the said Miscellaneous Appeal has adversely affected the right, title and interest of the petitioner and hence the petitioner has filed this Revisional Application challenging the Pre-emption Order dated 30-8-2001. 

 6. The petitioner before filing of this Revisional Application as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 61 of 2003 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur for declaration that the judgment and Order dated 30-8-2001 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 1998 is ineffective and not binding upon the petitioner. The learned Joint District Judge vide its judgment and decree dated 29-1-2007 (decree signed on 5-2-2007) dismissed the said suit on the ground that the petitioner cannot get relief in the suit since he did not challenge the judgment and Order dated 30-8-2001 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 1998 before Higher Court by way of Revision. The learned Judge of the trial Court also found that the suit is not maintainable since the deed of exchange in between the petitioner and opposite party No. 2 was executed during the pendency of the case. 

 7. The pre-emptor-opposite party No. 1 before filing of the original Miscellaneous (Pre-emption) Case No. 17 of 1996 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 63 of 1996 before the Assistant Judge, Court No. 4, Gazipur for declaration that the deed of exchange being No. 4346 dated 1-8-1995 (against which Pre-emptor field Pre-emption case) is a sell deed. In the said suit the Pre-emptor (opposite party No. 1 herein) as plaintiff claimed that the impugned deed of exchange was executed only with the view to prevent the right of the pre-emption. After conclusion of the trial learned Assistant Judge, Court No. 4, Gazipur by judgment and decree dated 22-9-1997 (decree signed on 1-10-1997) dismissed the said suit holding that the plaintiff having failed to prove her case that the impugned deed of exchange was a deed of sale. 

 9. Mr AFM Mesbahuddin, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner at the very outset upon referring to the decisions reported in 49 DLR (AD) 151, PLD 1984 (SC) 166 and 21 DLR (SC) 50 submits that though the petitioner was not party in the original pre-emption case as well as pre-emption miscellaneous appeal but in the facts and circumstance of the case the petitioner has right to protect his right, title and interest by filling Revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure since the impugned judgment and Order adversely affected right, title and interest. 

 10. Mr Mesbahuddin, the learned Advocate on the point of maintainability of the Revisional application submits that the Revisional power of the High Court is a supervisory power which may also be exercised suo moto and any person is competent to bring an illegality into the notice of the High Court and there is no bar of this Court sitting under revisional jurisdiction to rectify the illegality on such information and, as such, in the facts and circumstance of the case this revisional application is well maintainable since the Court of appeal below ignoring a decree passed by a competent Civil Court abruptly arrived at a finding in a summary pre-emption proceeding that the deed in question was out and out sale deed though the learned Assistant Judge on an elaborate discussion of the entire materials on record dismissed Title Suit No. 63 of 1996 by its judgment and decree dated 22-9-1997 (decree signed on 1-10-1997) with the observation that the deed in question was not a deed of sale which was, in fact, an exchange deed. 

 11. Referring to the judgment and Order passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Gazipur in Pre-emption Misc. Case No. 17 of 1996 the learned Advocate submits that the learned Assistant Judge rightly disallowed the pre-emption case by his judgment and Order dated 20-4-1998 on the findings that the pre-emptor before filing of the Pre-emption Case No. 17 of 1996 filed Title Suit No. 63 of 1996 before the Assistant Judge, Court No. 4, Gazipur for declaration that the deed of exchange being No. 4346 dated 1-8-1995 (against which Pre-emptor filed the Pre-emption case) is out and out sell deed, not a deed of exchange which was executed as deed of exchange only with the view to prevent the right of the Pre-emption which was dismissed on contest vide judgment and decree dated 22-9-1997 (decree signed on 1-10-1997) and in that view of the matter there is no legal scope to reconsider a decided issue as to the question whether the deed in question was sale or exchange. 

 12. Mr AFM Mesbahuddin, while elaborating his submission upon placing the judgment and decree dated 22-9-1997 passed in Title Suit No. 63 of 1996, judgment and Order dated 20-4-1998 passed in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 1996, judgment and Order dated 30-8-2001 passed in Miscellaneous (Pre-emption) Appeal No. 27 of 1998, judgment and decree dated 29-1-2005 passed in Title Suit No. 61 of 2003 and judgment and decree dated 6-6-2005 passed in Title Appeal No. 33 of 2005 by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur submits that in any event the lower appellate Court acted wrongly and illegally in setting-aside the judgment of the trial Court giving a go by to a unchallenged decree over the self same issue passed by a competent Civil Court in accordance with law and, as such, at any rate the impugned judgment and Order is liable to be set aside. 

 13. Mr Al Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No.1, on the other hand, supports the impugned judgment and Order dated 30-8-2001 which was, according to him just, correct and proper. Mr Mohammad Ali, in the course of his argument after placing the judgments of two Courts below and other relevant materials on record submits that the instant Civil Revision is misconceived and also not maintainable inasmuch as the petitioner was neither a party in appeal not in the original pre-emption case, who as like as a stranger filed this instant Revisional application challenging the impugned judgment and Order dated 30-8-2001. 

 14. He further submits that this petitioner earlier plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 63 of 1996 challenging the impugned judgment and Order dated 30-8-2001 passed by the learned District Judge, Gazipur in Miscellaneous (Pre-emption) Appeal No. 27 of 1998 and thereafter preferred Title Appeal No. 33 of 2005 and after being unsuccessful in both the suit and appeal as 3rd party stranger preferred this Revisional application against the said judgment and Order 30-8-2001 passed by the learned District Judge, Gazipur in Title Appeal No. 27 of 1998. Mr Mohammad Ali, further submits that there is nothing on record to show that the predecessor-in-interest of the present petitioner taken any ground in their written objection or their evidence that the case was barred by law of res-judicata as such the Court of appeal below as last Court of fact committed no illegality in allowing the Pre-emption. 15 

 16. The petitioner's case is that petitioner having acquired the case property by way of an exchange deed, mutated his name and has been enjoying the said land by erecting a two-storied building thereon. The petitioner was no aware about the Pre-emption case as well as the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 2998 who 29-5-2002 for the first time on getting a notice issued by Mouchak Police Sub-station, Kaliakoir came to know that the opposite party No.1 therein as pre-emptor obtained a Pre-emption Order in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 1998 against the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioner namely Md Abdul Hakim Talukder, who is opposite party No. 2 herein. The said Pre-emption Order dated 30-8-2001 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 1998 has adversely affected the rightly, title and interest of the petitioner and as such the petitioner has filed this Revisional Application challenging the Pre-emption Order dated 30-8-2001 though, the petitioner was neither party in the Pre-emption case nor he was made party in the Pre-emption Misc appeal. 

 20. As I have already noticed that impugned judgment and Order of Pre-emption dated 30-8-2001 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 1998 has adversely affected the right, title and interest of the petitioner though, the petitioner was neither party in the original Pre-emption case nor in the pre-emption Misc appeal. Therefore, in the facts and circumstances of the case and the principles laid down in the decisions as cited above, I have no hesitation to hold that the instant Revisional application is well maintainable. Besides, no top of that the Revisional power of the High Court Division is supervisory power which may also be exercised suo motu. 

 22. The opposite party No. 1 as pre-emptor filed Pre-emption Misc. Case No. 17 of 1996 for pre-empting the land measuring 59 decimals of land in SA Khatian No. 248/288 under Mouza-Shakashar, PS Kaliakoir, District-Gazipur as described in Deed No. 4336 dated 1-8-1995 on the allegation that the pre-emptor-opposite party No. 1 is a co-sharer to the case jote inheritance, after the death of her father her sister, Monwara Begum transferred her share to pre-emptee-opposite party No. 1 beyond the knowledge of the pre-emptor by executing Deed No. 4336 dated 1-8-1995. The opposite party Nos. 1-2 in Order to defeat the right or pre-emption collusively and cunningly described the deed of transfer a deed of exchange. The pre-emptee-opposite party No.1 is a stranger to the case jote and as such the pre-emptor is entitled to pre-empt the land. 

 (5) Whether the pre-emptor is entitled to get the land by way of pre-emption? 

 (6) Whether the pre-emption is entitled to get any other relives? 

 25. The trial Court below upon hearing both the sides and on considering the materials on record disallowed the Pre-emption case mainly on 2 (two) counts that: (i) the Pre-emptor-opposite party No. 1 having failed to prove that the deed in question was and out (5) sale deed and (ii) it has been decided earlier in Title Suit No. 63 of 1996 that the deed in question was a deed of exchange, not a sale deed. 

 27. On a close examination of evidence of PWs and OPWs, I do not find any reliable or corroborative evidence on record to suggest that the pre-emptee-opposite party No. 2, Monwara Begum, sister of the pre-emptor-opposite party sold the case land by executing the kabala in question. Moreover, the opposite party after being unsuccessful to prove that the deed in question was a sale deed in Title Suit No. 63 of 1996 as pre-emptor filed the instant case for pre-emption disputing the self same issue that the deed in question was out and out sale deed without challenging the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge in Title Suit No. 63 of 1996. Thus, it appears that so long a valid decree passed by a competent Court on contest against the plaintiff stands the same is binding on him who is present pre-emptor of Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 1996.
