caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 227 of 2006
parties:
Sree Santash Kumar Sarker and another ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Sree Shanker Chandra Mondal and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Facts, leading to this petition, are that the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 filed a suit being Other Class Suit No.102 of 1991 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Rajshahi against the petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 and respondent Nos.3-5 for cancellation of the compromise decree dated 25-10-1998 of Title Appeal No.251 of 1996 passed by the Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) Rajshahi and also for a declaration of title stating that the suit land originally belonged to Nitai, Gopal, Nirmal, Ajit, Krishnapada and Subhadra Rani, who sold the suit properties in favour of Sita Nath and Profulla Bala in 1976, who obtained possession. The said Sita Nath and Profulla was husband and wife, who had no child therefore in order to retain the lineage of inheritance they adopted Nitai Chandra Mondal, father of the plaintiff-petitioners in 1964 and thus Nitai Chandra Mondal came to the house of Sita Nath and remain there and being reared up as son and after the attainment of marriageable age Nitai Chandra Mondal was married with defendant No.3 and took her to live with Nitai Chandra Mondal in the house of Sita Nath. Thereafter, Sita Nath died leaving adopted son Nitai Chandra Mondal and his wife Profulla Bala. After the death of Sita Nath under advice of local Matbars, Profulla Bala registered a deed of gift in favour of plaintiffs on 09-12-1982. Thereafter, Profulla Bala died leaving Nitai Chandra Mondal and he (plaintiff) used to posses the suit properties exclusively to the exclusion of defendant opposite-parties for more than 12 years. The defendant-opposite-party Nos. 1 and 2 with a view to grab the suit properties filed a suit being Other Class Suit No.238 of 1983 in the Court of Munsif, Sadar at Rajshahi giving a false statement that they are close relations of Sita Nath and Profulla Bala and created a forged deed. Thereafter, the suit was transferred in the Court of Assistant Judge at Paba and was renumbered as Other Class No.279 of 1984 and the suit was dismissed on contest. Thereafter, defendant-opposite-parties preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No.249 of 1986 and then during the pendency of the appeal Nitai Chandra Mondal died leaving 2 sons and a wife and 4 daughters. When Nitai Chandra Mondal died then the plaintiff petitioners were minors and as such guardian of the minors and mother, defendant No.3 used to contest the appeal. During the period their mother, became morally weak and she acted against the benefit of the minors and that the minors became day labourer and they were reared up as servant in other family and their mother changed religion and acted to the determent of the interest of the minors and their mother was a widow, illiterate, immoral and later on changed religion and for that she acted in the hands of the defendants and then defendants were able to allure her and obtained a fraudulent solenama. She was not given independent advice. On 25-03-1991, a man of defendant No.1 disclosed that the Title Appeal No.249 of 1986 was decreed in favour of the defendants on compromise then the petitioners came to know that very soon the defendants would take possession of the suit properties. Thereafter, they obtained the certified copy of the sole decree dated 15-10-1989 and filed the suit. 

 3. The defendant-petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing joint written statement denying all the material averments of the plaint and alleged that the suit is not maintainable in its present form, the suit is barred by limitation and also bad for defect of parties. The specific case of the defendant-opposite-party   Nos. 1 and 2, in short, is that the suit land originally belonged to Nitai, Gopal, Nirmal, Ajit, Krishnapada and Subhadra, who sold the suit properties by registered kabala dated 18-12-1996 in favour of their maternal aunt of the defendants and she after purchase erected dwelling house, paid rent and possessed for her. The said Profulla Bala while constructing his house gifted the suit properties in their favour and delivered possession and thereafter, they completed the unfinished work of confections by their own money. Profulla Bala on 24-08-1982 executed a deed of gift and registered on 21-12-1982. After execution of the deed her hand was fractured and for that before 21-12-1982 she could not register the deed and in this way the defendants acquired title. On 28-02-1983, Profulla Bala died issue less and these defendants performed all the funeral functions of Profulla Bala. The plaintiff’s father tried to dispossess the defendants and then the defendants filed Title Suit No.238 of 1983 and thereafter, the suit was transferred in the Assistant Judge, Puba and was renumbered as 279 of 1984 and the same was dismissed. Then the defendant preferred an appeal before the District Judge, Rajshahi being Title Appeal No. 249 of 1986 which was transferred in the Court of Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Rajshahi and then the mother of the plaintiff-defendant No.3 of that suit on behalf of her minor sons and daughters compromised the suit for their benefit and as such the suit was decreed on compromise in favour of the defendant-opposite parties and the mother of the plaintiff-defendant No.3 took Tk.60,000/- as selenium. The plaintiffs have got no title and possession and therefore the suit is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 4. The trial Court upon examining both oral and documentary evidence on record decreed the suit against which, the defendant-petitioners preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No.251 of 1996 and the plaintiff respondent preferred another appeal being Title Appeal No.25 of 1997 and both the appeals were heard analogously by the Additional District Judge, Rajshahi, who upon hearing both sides allowed the Title Appeal No.251 of 1996 and dismissed the Title Appeal No.25 of 1997.
case_type_name: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal

parties:
Abdul Gafur (Md)  ----- Petitioner
vs
Mozaher Ali Pramanik  and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
2. Facts, relevant for the purpose of disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the petitioner as plaintiff on 30-9-1986 instituted Other Class Suit No. 28 of 1986 in the Court of the Royganj Upazila Assistant Judge, under District Serajganj for declaration of his title in respect of the suit land comprising of Plot Nos. 2952, 2953 and 2955 of Mouza Erandor under PS Royganj of District Serajgonj stating, inter alia, that the suit property was originally owned and possessed by Tomej Mondal and Shukur Ali and while they were owning and possessing the suit land, they sold the same to Monsob Ali on 8-1-1926 by registered sale deed; that said Monsob Ali died leaving five sons namely, Soken Ali, Kashem. Ali, Hazrat Ali, Kerob Ali and Salauddin to inherit the suit land. While they were thus owning and possessing they transferred the suit land on 27-6-1966 by registered sale deed No. 5948 to Ayesan Ali who thereafter transferred the same on 30-1-1980 to the plaintiff-petitioner by registered sale deed No. 1763; that the plaintiff-petitioner thus by becoming owner in possession by purchase recorded his name in the RS Khatian and on going to the office of the concerned Assistant Commissioner (Land) on 10-5-1986 for mutation, found that names of Monzil Sarker and Karom Ali had been wrongly recorded in the SA Khatian without any basis; that those two persons had no right, title, interest and possession over the suit land and, as such, the said SA record is wrong and illegal, that by the wrong record of right the title of the plaintiff-petitioner in the suit property has been clouded. As such he filed the said OC Suit No.28 of 1986 for clearing the cloud over his title on the suit property. 

 3. That the original defendants, the heirs of SA recorded tenant Monzil Sarker and Karom Ali (the opposite parties Nos. 2(a) to 2(g) and 3(a) to 3(h) did not contest in the suit, but the added defendant No.3, the opposite party No.1, who is also elder brothel of the plaintiff-petitioner, contested the suit by filing written statements on 26-10-1989 stating, amongst others, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form, the suit is barred by limitation and suffers from defect of parties. He admitted the ownership upto Monsob Ali but thereafter he stated that said Monsob Ali ceased his ownership over the suit property by abandoning his tenancy right by way of oral Istafanama to the superior landlord Ashutosh Lahiri who thereafter orally settled the suit land to one Sober Khan, that the tenancy of the superior landlord Ashutosh Lahiri was put into auction for non-payment of rent and a Certificate Case No. 101 of 1935-36 started against the said superior landlord; that Sober Khan being in possession over the suit property paid all the arrear rents to protect the property from public auction sale; that Sober Khan thus while was owning and possessing the suit land sold the same on 2-10-1945 in favour of three brothers Monjila Sarker, Injil Sarker and Karom Ali. Injil Sarker died leaving behind the aforesaid two brothers and as such the SA record was correctly recorded in their names; that out of the said two brothers Karom Ali died leaving three sons namely (1) Sohrab Ali (2) Abdul Wahab and (3) Abdul Latif; that the aforesaid three sons of Karom Ali and Monzil Sarker jointly sold out the suit property on 5-10-1983 to the opposite party No.1 by registered sale deed and thus the opposite party No.1 by becoming owner-in-possession mutated his name in the office of the Assistant Commissioner of Land and has been paying rents thereof to the Government; that the learned Assistant Judge, Royganj Upazila, Serajgonj framed six issues and decided the issue Nos. 2 and 3 in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner stating that the suit does not suffer from defect of parties and not barred by limitation; he decided other four issues analogous and dismissed the suit on contest against the defendant No.3 and ex parte against the rest despite the evidences on record and contrary to the law involved in the case seriously prejudicing the plaintiff-petitioner. 

 5. That the plaintiff-petitioner though has proved his case by producing the original documents 30 years old made those documents Exhibits as Exhibits Nos.1 to 6 (ka) and proved the aforesaid Exhibit by oral evidences, the Assistant Judge, Royganj illegally brushed aside those evidences by misconstruing them. Moreover, the learned Assistant Judge, Royganj dismissed the suit against the oral evidences by coming to an arbitrary decision. 

 7. Mr TM Shakil Hasan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, has submitted that the learned Appellate Judge affirmed the judgment and decree of the Trial Court on an erroneous basis without properly going through the evidence on record and thus he committed an error of law leading to error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, as such, the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside. He further submits that the learned Appellate Judge affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court without categorically discussing the evidence on record and specially without taking into consideration the factum of the claim of acquisition of title of the contesting opposite party No.1 which he claimed by way of Istofanama by the original owner in favour of the Zaminder without producing any documentary evidence or any witnesses to that effect and the Trial Judge contradicted himself in his own finding, in this regard and dismissed the suit of the plaintiff and the Appellate Judge also committed error of law leading to error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by upholding the aforesaid judgment and decree of the trial Court without properly evaluating the evidences-on-record in this respect. The next point of submissions as made by Mr Shakil Hasan that the learned Trial Judge as well as the Appellate Judge committed error of law by disbelieving the two dakilas filed in the Court by the plaintiff being Exhibit 4 and 4 Ka and thus committed error of law in arriving at the decision which has caused failure of justice. 

 8. Mr Shakil has further submitted that the learned Assistant Judge committed serious error by making attachment notice issued by the Certificate Officer without the same being formally proved and making the same as Exhibit Kha and by putting reliance upon the same believed the case of the defendants and dismissed the case of the plaintiff and the learned Appellate Judge committed error of law leading to error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by accepting the same. In this connection Mr Shakil Hasan has drawn my attention to Annexure-A with his Rule petition and he submits that in view of the Annexure-A which speaks of total falsity of the aforesaid Exhibit Kha of the defendant and because of non appearance of the learned Advocate for the appellant at the time of hearing of the appeal this document could not be produced before the appellate Court, as such, this Court may take into consideration this information slip and the case may be remanded to the Courts below for consideration of this fact as per law which will change the decision arrived at by the Courts below. Because the plaintiff has good title by several registered deeds starting from 1926 to 1980 from the original owner having good chain of transfer of case land in favour of the plaintiff, inasmuch as the plaintiff has produced draft copy of the RS Khatian which stands in his name in respect of the case property but both the Courts below did not properly evaluate this document. He prays that the rule be made absolute.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 723 of 2005
parties:
K.K.K. Garments Limited------ Petitioner.
-Vs-
Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited and others.------ Respondent.
full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff-respondents instituted Title Suit No. 239 of 1997 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka alleging, inter alia, that the plaintiff   is a public limited banking company incorporated in Bangladesh under the Companies Act, 1913 and carrying on banking business under Islamic Shariah Law with its registered head office at Motijheel, Dhaka, Defendant No.1 is a limited company and defendant No. 2 is managing Director and defendant Nos. 3 and 4 acre directors of the said company. The defendant Company opened current account No. 1418 with the plaintiff bank and the plaintiff bank sanctioned loan to defendant No.1 on Murabha investment basis for a sum of Tk. 20,14,087.00 for machinery and the defendants accepted the sanction letter which is fixed for repayment of the loan money together with profits thereof by 28.04.1988. Defendant Nos. 2 and 3 deposited the deed of the schedule property as collateral security in favour of the plaintiff bank and also executed and registered separate power of attorney. Over and above, the defendants deposited the memorandum, title deed, affidavit, power of attorney, deed of agreement and other connected documents together with original documents as collateral security. Defendants also executed promissory note, demand promissory note, letter of disbursement, letter of guarantee and other charged documents along with hire purchase agreement. The defendant deposited Tk. 10,00,000.00 (ten lac) only T.D.R. to the plaintiff bank, but the defendants did not repay the murabaha investment amount which stood at Tk. 28,19,149.00 on 28.04.1988 and on the prayer of the defendants the said amounts were turned into hire purchase grant on 13.08.1990. The defendants failed and 31 neglected to pay the bank dues in time and subsequently the hire purchase grant was re-scheduled by the plaintiff bank several times, the project loan again was turned into hire purchase sirkatul mulk at the request of the defendants, the defendants executed the agreement accordingly but the defendants did not pay the said amount till 31.01.1997. The plaintiff bank would get Tk. 73,51,363.00 as against hire purchase investment. The plaintiff bank granted composite investment to the defendant for Tk. 2,50,00,000.00 out of which Tk. 2,00,000,00.00 (two crores) were earmarked for L/C. and Tk. 50,00,000.00 for pre-shipment investment and the loan in question was re-schedule as per prayer of the defendants. The defendants did not manufacture any garment but sold away the fabrics so imported and misappropriated the money. The date of repayment was fixed on 28.04.1988, but the defendants failed to repay the bank's dues, inspite of request of the defendants the business of the defendants was turned into hire purchase on 13. 08.1990 and availed all the facility of composite investment with re-scheduling, but the defendants failed to pay inspite of written notice on series of dates. Defendant No.1 is the beneficiary and the other defendants axe the guarantors. So, all the defendants are individually and collectively liable to pay the bank due the profits of the principal amount and other expenses amounting to Tk. 2,56,38,277.00. The plaintiff bank exhausted all process to realize the bank dues from the defendant respondents, but the defendant-respondents did not repay the amount due to the plaintiff bank. The cause of action for the suit arose lastly on 24.04.1997 and as such, the plaintiff bank has been forced to take the shelter of law for recovery of its good money amounting to Tk. 2,56,28,277.00 together with up-to-date interest @ 18% till realization of the decreetal amount. 

 3. The petitioners as defendants contested the suit filing a written statement alleging, inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable, false, fraudulent, frivolous, fictitious, malafide and concocted one and as such, the present suit is liable to be dismissed summarily. Defendants case is that the plaintiff bank sanctioned loan to the defendant No. 1 on 25.07.1984 for a sum of Tk. 20,14,087.00 and the defendants accepted the grant by admitting all the terms and conditions, the time was fixed on 28.04.1988 for repayment of the loan money together with the profits thereon, defendant Nos. 2 and 3 deposited title deeds, affidavit, deed of agreement and other connected documents together with the original documents in usual course of banking system. In course of whole transaction the defendants demanded for a number of time the statement of account of the principal amount so far paid by the defendants to the plaintiff bank but until now the same was not supplied by the plaintiff bank for which the defendant could not make out his case with distinctive ratio and with the passing of time the machinery lost the workable capacity, the defendants requested the plaintiff bank for further importation of machinery under BMRE but the plaintiff refused the proposal. It is an contractual obligation in the part of the plaintiff bank to extend financial assistance as and when the defendants factory and business is required and in the meantime the defendants mortgaged all their properties up to the last inch to the plaintiff bank. The most important aspect in the whole episode is that the plaintiff bank deliberately kept all the documents of the defendants in custody and the properties mortgaged. So, all avenues for the defendants were closed to tide over the situation by giving further mortgage to any other bank and thereby to keep the factory running. The suffocating situation was created by the plaintiff bank resulting at tremendous loss for which the plaintiff bank is exclusively responsible. 

 4. Mr. Md. Nawab Ali, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division. committed error of law in allowing the appeal and thereby setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court without averting the findings of the trial Court as per mandatory provisions of Rule 31 of order XXXXI of Code of Civil Procedure and as such, the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside. He further submitted that the High Court Division found that "in the circumstances it appears that the Court below arrived at an erroneous decision in decreeing the suit-in-part. The trial Court made different arithmetical calculations to settle the liability for the respondents entirely at his I own accord without any nexus with the statement of accounts and several exhibits produced for proving the liabilities of the respondents and as such the plaintiff-appellant bank is entitled to get a decree for the claimed amount" which on the face of it, is without any reason and basis and therefore committed error of law and as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. 

 5. The learned Advocate further submitted that there are three other heads namely, bills of Tk. 97,54,730.00 (ninety seven lac fifty four thousand seven hundred thirty), PSI of Tk. 29,01,011.00 (twenty nine lac one thousand eleven) and B.B bills TK. 55,11,000.00 (fifty five lac eleven thousand) but there was no assertion in the plaint how these loans have been created; furthermore, from the statement of account submitted by the respondent bank it is evident that the petitioner has executed. export order through different L.C. amounting to Tk. 11,65,00,000.00 (eleven crore sixty five lac) and the responde bank has paid the import dues amounting to Tk. 10,79,00,000.00 (ten crore seventy nine lac) and as all the exportation and importation has been carried on through respondent who debted Tk. 10,73,00,000.00 (ten crore seventy three lac) from the repatriated sale proceed from the account of the petitioner and as such, only Tk. 6,00,000.00 (six lac) remained unpaid. The said specific finding of the trial Court based on statement of account submitted by the respondent bank was neither reversed by the High Court Division nor any finding was given to that effect refer-ring to the exhibit and statements of account. He further submitted that trial Court after appraisal of materials on record held that under the head of project loan the plaintiff respondent claim Tk. 62,03,387.90 (sixty two lac three thousand three hundred eighty seven and paisa ninety) and in three different heads Tk. 6,00,000.00 (six lac) and, as such, the petitioner respondent is entitled to total Tk. 68,03,387. 90 (sixty eight lac three thousand three hundred eighty seven and paisa ninety) P.W.1 admitted that the plaintiff repaid Tk. 28,00,000.00 (twenty eight lac) during pendency of suit and therefore the respondent is entitled to Tk. 40,03,387.90 (forty lack three thousand three hundred eighty seven and paisa ninety) and the suit was decreed to that extent but the High Court Division failed to reverse the findings referring to the materials on record and as such, committed error of law and therefore, liable to be set aside. 

 6. Mrs. Sufia Khatun, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for the respondent No.1 submitted that the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat committed a grave error of law in decreeing the suit partially though the appellant has proved the case by sufficient evidence both oral and documentary and, as such, the appellant is legally entitled to get a decree for the entire claimed amount. 

 8. The High Court Division while allowing the appeal with modification of the judgment and decree of the trial Court observed that the Court below arrived at an erroneous decision in decreeing the suit-in-part. It also appears that the trial Court made different arithmetical calculation to settle the liability for the petitioners entirely at its own accord without any nexus with the statement of accounts and several exhibits produced for proving the liabilities of the petitioners and, as such, the plaintiff bank is entitled to get a decree for the claimed amount. The trial Court came to an erroneous finding to the effect the plaintiffs' claim of Tk. 74,71,536.00 in unreasonable which has misled it to dismiss the major claim of the Bank and anomalously the trial Court had decreed the suit-in-part.

caseno: Civil Appeal No. 330 of 2003 with Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 645 of 2001
parties:
Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Environment and Forests and others ----- Appellants
Vs.
Md Ayub Ali and anthers ----- Petitioners
full_judgment:
3. The plaintiffs filed the aforesaid suit (Other Suit No. 20 of 1993) in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Birampur, Dinajpur for a declaration that the suit land measuring 4.75 acres of land is comprised of a mango garden having 74 mango trees standing thereon is not a forest land and, as such, the vesting of control and management thereof in the Forest Department are illegal and inoperative and not binding on the plaintiffs and the plaintiffs are entitled to reversion of the same free from control and management of the Forest Department on the following allegations. 

 4. The suit land including the mango garden originally belonged to the CS recorded tenant, Ramani Kanta Sarkar, who planted the mango trees on the suit land. After his death, his three sons transferred 2.85 acres of land to the plaintiffs by the kabala dated 24-5-1958. On 28-5-1958 CS recorded tenant's successive heirs sold 95 decimals of land to the plaintiffs and on 28-9-1959 three successive heirs of the CS recorded tenant sold 95 decimals of land to the plaintiffs and thus in the aforesaid manner the plaintiffs acquired the suit land. During revisional survey a part of the suit land was recorded in the name of the plaintiffs and a portion of the suit land was recorded in the name of the successive heirs of the said CS recorded tenant whose shares were subsequently purchased in the name of the plaintiffs by their father when they were minor and possession of the land so purchased was made over to the plaintiffs father. During the war of liberation plaintiffs father and some other relatives were killed and because of such disaster plaintiffs were in a perplexed state of mind and, as such, they had difficulty in exercising effective control over the suit land. In the middle of July, 1990 while the officials of the Forest Department came to pluck mango, the plaintiffs protested to that and they then came to know for the first time that the Forest Department acquired the control and management of  the suit land by a notification under the Private Forests Act, 1945. It is also alleged that neither the plaintiffs nor their predecessors-in-interest had any knowledge about the gazette notification vesting control and management of the suit land in the Forest Department nor any notice was ever served on them to show cause against such vesting. It is also asserted by the plaintiffs that the suit land is a mango garden from a long time past and it was neither a private forest nor a waste land. Hence, the taking over, control and management of the suit land under the Private Forests Act, 1945 and also under the Forests Act, 1927 was illegal. The plaintiffs accordingly, made a representation to the Ministry of Forest on August 9, 1990 to return the suit land to them but received no response. The plaintiffs thereafter represented to the Deputy Commissioner, Dinajpur on 4-1-1992 for handing over the management of the mango garden to them but did not have the desired result. The plaintiffs then represented to the Forest Department for releasing the suit land and thereupon a report was called for and the date of hearing was fixed on 30-3-1992 in this regard. But the Forest Department at the same time also fixed 28-3-1992 for auction of the mango garden. The plaintiffs having found no prospect of release of the suit land filed the suit. 

 5. The defendant Nos. 1-3 and 5 contested the suit by filing joint written statement denying the material allegations contending, inter alia, that since the owners of the suit land failed to raise any objection pursuant to the notices issued on them under the Private Forests Act, the Government by issuing notification dated 3-6-1958 under sections 7 and 11 of the said Act vested control of the suit land in the Regional Forest Officer and since then the defendants have been treating the suit land as a vested forest and continuing to manage the same. The Forest Department thereafter regularly put the said mango garden on auction between 1976-1993. The plaintiffs, however, made representations to the Deputy Commissioner, Dinajpur as well as to the Ministry of Forest for release and return of the suit land to them but their prayer was turned down. The plaintiffs have no title, interest and possession in the suit land and accordingly they manufactured false documents and filed the suit with a view to grabbing the suit land. 

 8. The short fact leading to the filing of the aforesaid Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 645 of 2001 is that the respondents, Md Nazibar Rahman Talukder and others, as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 178 of 1977 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Rangpur for declaration of plaintiffs' title to the suit land measuring 25.32 and 2.73 acres as described in the schedule Ka and Kha to the plaint. The suit land originally belonged to Taher Mahmud and Hanif Mahmud. The plaintiffs are the heirs and lineal descendants of the said original owners, Taher Mahmud and Hanif Mahmud. The plaintiffs have been owning and possessing the suit land as per their respective share by amicable arrangement among themselves. The suit land was jungle land and the same was so described in CS Khatian and recorded in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs. Ultimately, the plaintiffs and their co-sharers cleared the jungle of the suit land in the year 1348 BS and made the same a cultivable land and since then the plaintiffs have been in possession of the same by amicable arrangement amongst themselves and with other co-sharers. The plaintiffs came to know on 3-9-1977 when the government attempted to lease out the suit land on the pretext that the government by notification under the Private Forests Act, 1945 took over the suit land for proper management and control as private forest. The plaintiffs did not know about the said notification and they were and still are in possession of the suit land. But the Karmacharies of the defendants collusively got the suit land recorded in the name of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in the SA record. After knowing about the wrong SA record in the name of the said defendants in the government, the plaintiffs in the first part of 1973 filed a Miscellaneous Case No. 26 of 1973 under section 143(A) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which was dismissed for default on 15-6-1976 due to illness of the plaintiff No. 1 as tadbirkarak. Plaintiff No. 1 after recovery from his illness tried to file a Miscellaneous Case for setting aside the said ex parte order of dismissal but due to legal complications the plaintiffs did not file the Miscellaneous Case but instead filed the present suit for declaration of their title in respect of the suit land. 

 9. The defendant Nos. 1-3 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the suit-land was a forest land up to 1972 and during the war of liberation the plaintiffs and their relations entered into the forest land, cut down the trees and cleared the jungles and made an attempt to cultivate the same for which several cases were filed in the Court of the SDM Rangpur. The defendants took steps to evict the illegal occupants including the plaintiffs from the suit land but they did not succeed in their attempt in evicting the plaintiffs from the suit land. The plaintiffs are illegal occupants in the suit land since 1971. The defendant No.1 issued a notice to the owners to show cause as to why the suit land should not be vested in the government for the purpose of afforestation and after observing all formalities the government issued a notification No. 14253 dated 4-12-1953 vesting management and control of the suit land in the government. The Forest Department took over the possession of the suit land from 1953 and since then the government had been possessing the same. The plaintiffs or the original owners cannot legally claim any title or possession in the suit land. The plaintiffs are unauthorised occupants since 1971 and hence the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 10. The suit was decreed by the trial Court on contest against the contesting defendant Nos. 1-3 and ex parte against the rest declaring title to the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs vide its judgment and decree dated 15-6-1981. Thereafter, the defendants preferred first appeal in the High Court Division and the High Court Division dismissed the appeal by the impugned judgment on the ground that the suit is not barred by limitation, the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land and the defendant government has failed to prove producing any document or gazette notification under the Private Forests Act showing taking over or vesting of control and management of the suit land as forest or waste land for afforestation. In this background of the case, the defendants filed the present leave petition.

parties:
Shafiuddin Ahmed (Md) ----- Plaintiff-Appellant- Petitioner
vs
Basera Khatun alias Bachchu ----- Defendant-Respondent- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the defendant-respondent-opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 11-6-2000 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Rajbari, in Title Appeal No. 20 of 1996 affirming the judgment and decree dated 30-1-96 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Goalundo, Rajbari, in Title Suit No. 29 of 1994 should not be set aside. 

 2. The brief fact of the case is, that the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 29 of 1994 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Goalundo, Rajbari for declaration of title stating, inter alia, that the suit hind measuring, 18 decimal of land originally belonged, to Manu Mallick who mortgaged the said land along with other lands to Rajbari Bank Limited and the Bank purchased the said land through Execution Case No. 731 of 1934 by obtaining a sale certificate from the Court. Thereafter, on 15-1-1944 the plaintiff and his brother Hashmat Ali purchased the above mentioned land by a registered deed and on the same date the plaintiff and his brother sold out the said land to one Mozaharuddin by way of registered kabala deed. Thereafter, the plaintiff got .25 acres of land in Plot No. 940 and 18 decimal of land in Plot No. 922 by a registered pitta dated 29-1-1944 from the said Mozaharuddin and a kabuliat also executed and registered by the plaintiff in favour of Mozaharuddin for the above mentioned total 43 decimal of land on the same date and the reference regarding the said patta was recited in the kabuliat. Thereafter, Mozaharuddin sold out 12 decimal of land from CS Plot No. 912 by executing a registered sale deed dated 30-8-61 where the facts related to the Kabuli at executed by the plaintiff had also been mentioned or narrated. The suit land i.e. 18 acres of land in plot No. 922, is cartilage of the house of the plaintiff and the house was built on the Plot No. 914. The said land is ingress and egress of the plaintiff's house. The plaintiff garages his cattle in the suit land recently, on 15-4-89 corresponding to 2nd Baishakh, 1396 BS the defendant No. 1 through her husband started claiming the suit land baselessly and then plaintiff came to know about the A and RS khatian prepared wrongly in the name of the defendant. The defendant No. 1 has/had no right, title and possession in the suit land in spite of she claimed title in the suit land which constrained the plaintiff to institute the present suit. 

 3. That the defendant No. 1 respondent-opposite party No. 1 entered appearance and contested the suit by filing written statements denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia that the father of the defendant, No. 1 Abdul Ali Khalifa got the said land by way of pattan from Rajbari Bank Limited and RS Khatian No. 331 was prepared in the name of Abdul Ali Khalifa and he had been paying rent to the said bank for the land on the basis of owner and tenant of the relationship. Thereafter, the suit land was developed under the Government and during SA operation SA record was prepared accordingly, in the name of Abdul Ali Khalifa and he had been possessing the land by cultivating paddy and by cutting the same just before making over the possession of the suit land to defendant No. 1 by executing a registered deed dated 23-6-69. The defendant No.1 used the timber standing on the suit land and her maternal grandmother used to reside there. Presently, the brother of defendant No.1 Enayet Molla looks after the suit land as defendant No. 1 who is residing in Dhaka with her husband. There is no right, title and interest of the plaintiff in the suit land and the records of the suit land has correctly been prepared in the name of the defendant. The defendant No. 1 permitted the plaintiff to use the suit land as pathway to reach the road of Municipal Corporation. The suit has falsely been filed by the plaintiff which is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 4. The suit was heard by the learned Assistant Judge, Goalundo, Rajbari and on the basis of the evidence, both oral and documentary, and on the basis of rent receipt and other connected papers, after concluding the trial the learned Assistant Judge, Goalundo, Rajbari was pleased to dismiss the suit by his judgment and decree dated 30-1-96 holding, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form; the suit is barred by limitation and defect of parties and RS and SA khatian have correctly been prepared in the name of late Abdul Ali Khalifa having found him in possession of the suit land and that the plaintiff has no right, title and interest in the suit land and also plaintiff has got no exclusive possession in the suit land. 

 5. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Goal undo, Rajbari the plaintiff preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 20 of 1996 in the Court of learned District Judge, which on transfer, was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge, Rajbari who was pleased to dismiss the said appeal by his judgment and decree dated 11-6-2000 and 18-6-2000 respectively holding, inter alia, that it can safely be said that the SA. record was rightly prepared in the name of Abdul Ali Khalifa within the knowledge of the plaintiff and the finding of the trial Court was right and justified as such, he affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. 

 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Rajbari in Title Appeal No. 20 of 1996, he plaintiff-appellant-petitioner preferred the instant revisional application before the High Court Division and obtained the present Rule. 

 7. The learned Counsel Mr Syed Mokaddas Ali appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner filed a supplementary affidavit adding some new additional grounds to be treated as part of revisional application and submits that the Courts below failed to appreciate the evidence on record and the judgment of both lower appellate Court as well as the trial Court appears to be manifestly perverse affecting the merit of the case resulting failure of justice which is liable to be interfered by this Court. The learned Counsel further submits that the Courts below committed an error in law as well as on facts in deciding the title and possession of the suit land. The learned Courts below without considering the certified copy of the sale deed dated 15-1-1944 executed and registered by Rajbari Bank Limited in favour of the plaintiff which was exhibited as Exhibit 3. Thereafter the certified copy of the registered patta dated 29-1-1944 given by Mozaharuddin in favour of plaintiff Md Shafiuddin which was exhibited as Exhibit 3(A) and the certified copy of the registered kabuliat dated 29-1-1944 given by plaintiff Md Shafiuddin in favour of Mozaharuddin which was exhibited as Exhibit 3(b) and the certified copy of the sale deed dated 15-1-1944 given by plaintiff and another in favour of Mozaharuddin which was exhibited as Exhibit 3(C) the certified copy of the registered sale deed dated 31-8-1961 given by Mozaharuddin in favour of Md Hanifuddin which was exhibited as Exhibit 3(d) were proved by calling the original volumes from the office of the Faridpur District Registrar through PW 5 Abul Hashem Khan and such registered deeds and documents were genuinely executed and hence the tenancy right of the suit land passed to the plaintiff- petitioner. Next he submits that the defendant No. 1 admitted in paragraph No. 13 of the written statements that the CS recorded tenant Manu Mallick was the original owner of the suit land who mortgaged the said land along with other lands to Rajbari Bank Limited and subsequently bank purchased the same through Execution Case No. 731 of 1934 and obtained a sale certificate from the Court. On the other hand the defendant No. 1 claimed the suit land through settlement by the said Rajbari Bank Limited, but neither in the written statement nor in the deposition of DW 1 or any witnesses mentioned any date of such settlement and the defendant could not produce any scrap of paper with regard to the settlement of the suit land on the basis of which the defendant claimed the suit property. The defendant only submits that original deed of pat tan was burned during the liberation war but the defendant could not produce the certified copy or any papers showing that he took paltan from Rajbari Bank Limited. Next the learned Counsel submits that plaintiff examined as many as 5(five) witnesses in this case and defendant also examined 5 witnesses in this case to prove their respective cases but the plaintiff examined the natural, probable and independent witnesses who were neighbours and who categorically stated and corroborated the evidence of PW 1. The PW 4 Md Maznu Miah who is a neighbor of both plaintiff and defendant categorically stated in his evidence that the suit land had been possessed by the plaintiff by grazing his cattle and children of the plaintiff used to play in the suit land, plaintiff also used the suit land as pathway to the access of his house. In cross-examination by the defendant could not shake any of the witnesses and the plaintiff successfully proved the possession of the suit land by adducing evidence. On the other hand, all the five witnesses examined by the defendant are relations. DW 1 Enayet Molla, the full brother of the defendant was examined on behalf of defendant No.1 Most Basera Khatun who in his cross-examination admitted that he could not say when and how and on what date the patta was taken from Rajbari Bank by Abdul Ali Khalifa though he stated that Abdul Ali Khalifa subsequently executed the kabala deed on 23-6-1969 which was exhibited by him as Exhibite-5. Yead Ali and Asfakuddin were examined as DW 2 and DW 3 who were also relations of the defendant. One Abdul Kader, the attesting witness of the deed was examined as DW 4 who stated in his cross-examination that Most Basera Khatun purchased the suit land from her father by a consideration money of Taka 100. He also, admitted that when Basera Khatun purchased the suit land from her father by Taka 100 at that time she was unmarried then where from she got the money. Moniruzzaman was examined as DW 5 who stated in his examination-in-chief that he saw the defendant Abdul Ali Khalifa to possess the suit land but in cross-examination he admitted that Abdul Ali Khalifa died long before i.e. in the year 1975. The learned Counsel for the petitioner further submits that the Courts below did not at all assess the evidence on record properly with regard to the possession of the suit land and came to a wrong and erroneous finding that the defendant was in possession of the suit land but, as a matter of fact, the trial Court as well as the lower appellate Court bank upon the RS and SA khatian and came to the conclusion that if the defendant was not in possession of the suit land the record of SA and RS khatian would not be prepared in the name of the defendant. He further submits that the defendant in collusion with the settlement employee and Tahshilder managed to prepare the khatian in the name of the defendant but the defendant was not in actual possession of the suit land. The lower appellate Court and the trial Court without applying their judicial mind and without proper assessment of the evidence on record and by ignoring the certified copies of series of documents of 1944 showing the title and possession of the plaintiff most illegally dismissed the suit of the plaintiff which is liable to be interfered by this Court. The learned Counsel finally submits that since the original documents were lost during the liberation war the plaintiff submitted the certified copies of all the documents and to prove the genuineness called for the original volume from office of the Faridpur District Registrar through PW 5 Abul Hashem Khan. On the other hand, the defendant could not produce any scrap of paper in support of their claim over the suit land with regard to pattan. 

 "The law is now settled as to the extent of jurisdiction of the High Court Division under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure to interfere with the judgment of the Court of fact i.e. courts below. The High Court Division in exercise of its revisional jurisdiction is competent to interfere with the judgment of court below only when there is misreading and non-construction of evidence or there is misconstruction of document but when there is no misreading or no consideration of the evidence or when there is no misconstruction of document the High Court Division is not competent to interfere with the judgment of the court below. In the instant case the Courts of fact i.e. the appellate Court and the trial Court, on detailed discussion and consideration of the evidence arrived at the findings that the plaintiff No. 1 has right, title, and possession in the land in suit and the defendants case of taking settlement has not been proved and the dakhilas filed by the defendants in support of the case of taking settlement of the land in suit were not proved by competent, independent and disinterested witnesses. The finding of the High Court Division as regard the possession of the land in suit is not legally well founded". 

 10. Next he cited another decision in the case of Habibullah (Md) vs Sher Ali Khan and others reported in 57 DLR (AD) 55 it is held that "The High Court Division while exercising its revisional jurisdiction is competent to reverse the judgment of the courts below when the same has been made either upon misreading or non-consideration of the material evidence causing failure of justice". The learned, Counsel referred another decision in the case of Moslem Kha vs Alep Kha and others reported in 10 BLC 708 wherein it is stated that "In a suit for declaration of title and confirmation of possession, the trial Court mainly considered the deposition of the DWs ignoring the deposition of the PWs and material documentary evidence which was affirmed by the appellate Court but the High Court Division considered the deposition of the PWs and found that the petitioner had been possessing the suit land since 1966 and accordingly, the suit was decreed setting aside the judgments and decrees of the Courts below". The learned Counsel finally submits that the lower appellate Court and the trial Court committed error in law as well as on facts which arc manifestly perverse, there is serious misreading and non-consideration of material evidence affecting the merit of the case as such, the judgments and decrees passed by the lower appellate Court as well as by the trial Court call for interference by this Court. 

 11. On the other hand, the learned Counsel Mr Probir Neegi, appearing on behalf of the defendant-respondent-opposite party submits that the concurrent finding of facts cannot be disturbed unless it is manifestly perverse. The trial Court as well as the lower appellate Court is absolutely justified in dismissing the suit of the plaintiff because the plaintiff miserably failed to prove his possession over the suit land and, as such, the Courts below found that the suit is not maintainable and the suit is barred by limitation and it is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The Courts below rightly found that the plaintiff was not in possession of the suit land and in a suit for declaration the plaintiff cannot .seek any relief as such, the plaintiff ought to have filed a title suit with a prayer for recovery of khas possession. The learned Counsel further submits that the SA and RS Khatian was prepared long before but the plain- tiff did not take any steps for correction of the record if at all it would be wrongly prepared as such the suit of the plaintiff is barred by limitation. The learned Courts below rightly found that the suit was barred by limitation. The defendant examined as many as 5 (five) witnesses in this case to prove the right, title and possession of the suit land and all the DWs proved the case of the defendant with regard to the possession of the suit land. The learned Connsel next submits that both the Courts below concurrently found that the plaintiff Md Shafiuddin Ahmed and his brother Hashmat Ali purchased the suit land along with other land from Rajbari Bank on 15-1-1944 by way of registered deed and on the same day they sold the said property to one Mozaharuddin by a registered deed. Thereafter Mozaharuddin gave patta to the plaintiff by a registered deed dated 29-1-1944 and plaintiff also gave a registered kabuliat to Mozaharuddin on 29-1-1944. The learned Counsel submits that it appears to be an unusual transaction which creates a doubt and suspicion with regard to the genuineness of the document and for this reason the lower appellate Court as well as the trial Court disbelieved the documents. The finding of the Courts below are absolutely right and justified and it should not be disturbed in revision under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his contention the learned Counsel cited the case of Hazari Bala Sana and another vs Niron alias Niranjan Mondal and others reported in 1997 BLD (AD) 295 wherein it has been held that "It is a settled principle that the finding of facts, whether concurrent or not, arrived at by the Power appellate Court, which is the final Court of fact, is binding on the High Court Division, as a revisional to out except in certain well defined exceptional circumstances, such as non-consideration or misreading of the material evidence affecting the merit of the case. Finally, the learned Counsel submits that if the plaintiff would be in possession of the suit land certainly the RS and SA Khatian would be prepared in the name of the plaintiff and; as such, both the Courts below rightly observed that the plaintiff miserably failed to prove his right; title and possession over the suit land. Therefore the judgment passed by the Courts below do not call for any interference by this Court. 

 "If need not be said again that mere payment of rent to the Government on the strength of unfounded entry in the record of right will not create a valid tenancy in favour of the defendants and extinguish title if any of the plaintiff No.1". 

 13. The Courts below failed to apply their judicial mind to assess the evidence both oral and documentary on record properly as such came to a wrong finding and dismissed the suit of the plaintiff. Both the Courts below by misreading and non-consideration of the material evidence both oral and documentary affecting the merit of the case with regard to title and possession of the plaintiff and failed to come to a correct finding of the case which is liable to be interfered by this Court. The plaintiff in proving his title produced the certified copy of the title deed and called the volume from the District Registrar Office to prove the genuineness of the documents since the original document was lost during the liberation war. 'The plaintiff also proved his title and possession over the suit and by adducing evidence of disinterested and independent witnesses who could not be shaken in cross examination by the defendant as such the judgment' and decree passed by the Courts below is called for interference by this Court. In this connection I like to rely on the case of Habibullah (Md) vs Sher Ali Khan and others reported in 57 DLR (AD) 55 wherein it has been held that "The High Court Division while exercising its revisional jurisdiction is competent to reverse the judgment of the Courts below when the same has been made either upon misreading or non-consideration of the material evidence causing failure of justice. Another decision can also be cited in this connection in the case of Hussain Ahmed Chowdhury alias Ahmed Hossain Chowdhury and others vs Md Nurul Amin and others reported in 47 DLR (AD) 162 wherein it is stated that 

 14. It will not be out of place to cite another decision with regard to Registration Act, Section 60 of the Registration Act and sections 65(c), 68, 78 and 79 of the Evidence Act, in the case of Aboni Mohan Saha vs Assistant Custodian, Vested Property, Chandpur reported in 39 DLR (AD) 223 wherein it is held that the proof of certified copies and presumption as to genuineness of the same when a certified copy of the document is produced some sanctity of law is attested by the Evidence Act "Section 78 read with section 79 of the Evidence Act provides for the proof of' the certified copies and the presumption as to the genuineness of such certified copies. The plaintiff has given explanation that the original was burnt. 

 Section 65(c) provides for secondary evidence "When the original has been destroyed or lost, or when the party offering evidence of its contents cannot, for any other reason not arising from his own default or neglect, produce it in reasonable time." It is further provided in cases of (a), (c) and (d) that secondary evidence of the contents of the document is admissible when the certified copy was produced by the plaintiff of registered deed of gift. 

 15. In view of the discussion made above and the facts and circumstances of the case and also the legal position, the plaintiff is entitled to obtain a decree in his favour. I find that the lower appellate Court is absolutely wrong in dismissing the Title Appeal No. 20 of 1996 arising out of the judgment and decree dated 30-1-1996 and also the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Goalundo, Rajbari, in Title Suit No. 29 of 1994. The judgment and decree dated 11-6-2000 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Rajbari, in Title Appeal No. 20 of 1996 affirming the judgment and decree Gated 30-1-96 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Goalundo, Rajbari, in Title Suit No. 29 of 1994 is hereby set aside.

parties:
Wega Fashion Sweater (PVT) Ltd. represented by its M.D. Nurul Huda ------ Appellant
Vs.
Syed Sajeda Hossain & others ------ Respondents
&
Director Adjutant of Ansar & V.D.P. having its office at Tikatuly & others ------ Respondents

Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of land and others ------ Appellants
Vs.
Syeda Sajeda Hossain & others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
3. The respondent No. 8 (appellant in C.A. No. 62 of 2004) by filing affidavit-in-opposition contested the rule and controverted the material allegations made in the writ petition and further contended, inter alia, that the writ petition involved complicated questions of fact as to title and also as to possession and dispossession which could not be decided without filing a proper suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession and as such the writ petition is not maintainable. The MLO No.128/86 dated 13.05.1986 having been issued by the then Chief Martial Law authority, the same is protected under Act No.1 of 1986 and as such writ petition does not lie against the said MLO No.128/86 and no relief touching the decision of any matter relating to the said MLO can be given in the writ petition. The allegation that the writ petitioners are joint owners of 17 decimals of land out of 1.25 acres of land of C.S. Plot No.177 or otherwise in possession of the same upon mutation of their names and upon payment of rent and taxes and that they were illegally dispossessed on 16.10.2000 are all denied by the appellant. The further case is that the writ petitioners were not in possession and as such the question of dispossession by the appellant did not arise, the allegation in the writ petition to the effect that Mrs. Madlena D. Rozario purchased the land of C.S., Plot No.177 from the C.S. recorded tenants and had been in possession are not correct. The entire land of C.S. Plot No.177 under C.S. Khatian No.49 of Mouza Begunbari, P.S. Tejgaon, Dhaka with other lands of the same Mouza were requisitioned by Government by order dated 28.09.1995 and 25.02.1960 under section 3 of the East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition and Property Act, 1949 and the said property continued to be subject of requisition. Subsequently the same were acquired by the Government in L.A. Case No.16/1959-1960 and notice of acquisition was published in the official Gazette on 28.03.1968 and as such the land absolutely vested in the Government free from all encumbrances and the right, title and interest of the original owners extinguished. The allegation that the lands were subsequently de-requisitioned are false and concocted. Since the land having been acquired finally vested in the Government, the question of treating the same as vested property (enemy property) or releasing the same by the Ministry of land does not arise. There is no law authorizing the Government to release any land once it vested in the Government by acquisition according to law. It was further contended that the writ petitioners have no locus-standi to seek relief as prayed for in the writ petition. 

 4. The respondent No.1, Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Land and respondent No.5 Sub-Divisional Engineer, Public Works Department, Dhaka by filing joint affidavit-in-opposition contested the Rule denying the material allegations made in the writ petition and further contended that complicated questions of title and possession and dispossession being involved the writ petition is not maintainable. The C.S. plot No.177 of Mouza-Begunbari, P.S. Tejgaon, Dhaka is acquired land of the Government No.5 and the allegation of dispossession of the writ petitioners on 16.10.2000 is false. The vacant possession of the land in question had been delivered to the respondent No.8 of the writ petition (appellant in C.A. No. 62 of 2004) by the respondent No.5 of the writ petition on 12.10.2000. The papers and documents filed by the writ petitioners were manufactured with malafide intention to grab the Government property. 

 9. At the time of hearing of the appeal the learned Counsel for the appellants in C.A. Nos.62-64 of 2004 filed copy of gazette notification dated March 28, 1968 published in the Dacca Gazette part-1. It shows that by notification under Memo No. Dacca-No. Da-36/68/359-Reqn-15th March 1968 full of cadastral survey Plot No.177 along with other plots were acquired by the Government. The position of law is that once the property is acquired under sub-section (7) of section 5 of the (East Bengal) Emergency Requisition of property Act, 1948 (East Bengal Act XIII of 1948), the same vests absolutely in the Government free from all incumbents and the right title and interest, if any, of the previous owners are extinguished. Under the law (East Bengal Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 (East Bengal Act XIII of 1948) the government has no authority of release the property in favour of either the original owner or anybody else. The Government may also use such land for similar other public purpose. 

 12. Therefore since the writ petitioner's vendor had no right, title and interest and possession it the disputed land after final acquisition of the property in L.A. Case No.16 of 1959-60 as stated above, they had no saleable interest and the writ petitioner by purchase from them did not acquire any interest in the land.

parties:
Salina Begum ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Mojibur Rahman and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-10 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 13-11-2001 passed by the learned District Judge, 2nd Court, Narsingdi, in Title Appeal No. 43 of 2000 affirming the judgment and decree dated 21-11-99 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Monohardi, District-Narsingdi, in Title Suit No. 46 of 1996 and partly decreed the suit for preliminary partition. 

 2. The short fact of the case is that the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner as plaintiff instituted the suit for Partition being numbered as Title Suit No. 46 of 1996 before the Senior Assistant Judge, Monohardi, Narsingdi for partition of the suit land at Mouza Nischantapur, District-Narsingdi. The suit land originally belonged to Bhabani Kishore and Kailash Chandra Chakraborty respectively in CS Khatian No. 140, Whose name was also recorded properly in R,SKhatian No. 146. But during the SA operation for preparing the SA record wrongly recorded the name of one Deen Bandhu who has got no right and title in the suit land. Bhabani Kishore died leaving behind only one son Manik Kishore who became the absolute owner of the plot Nos. 70, 71 and 567. Thereafter, he sold .32 decimals of land out of 96 decimals to Abdul Hashem, the husband of the plaintiff, by a Deed No. 8235 dated 3-12-88 and registered in Monohardi Sub-Registry Office but in that deed the caste of the vendor and District were wrongly written. The caste was written Muslim instead of Hindu and the District was written Mohongonj instead of Munshigonj. The suit property pertaining to CS Khatian No. 141 originally belonged to Syed Obaidullah, Syed Azizullah, Syed Ahmed Ullah, Syed Rafiqullah, Syed Atikullah, Syed Sarafat Akhter, Syed Sara Akhter Khatoon, Syed Md Hafizullah whose name was also recorded in SA Khatian No. 146 correctly. Thereafter, Syed Rafiqullah was enjoying the suit property by amicable partition with his brothers and out of which Rafiqullah sold .35 decimals of land to Abul Hashem, the husband of the plaintiff, by a Registered Deed No. 8234 dated 3-12-88. The original registered deed was lost, as such, the certified copy of the same was submitted. 

 3. The suit property pertaining to 51 khatian originally belonged to and owned by Gour Kishore who died leaving behind 2(two) sons namely, Krishon Kishore and Harendra Kishore Das who orally gifted 32 decimals of land of Rafizuddin, the father of the plaintiff, on 10 Chaitra, 1365 BS. But due to restriction on registration of Hindu property the same property was gifted to Abul Hashem, the husband of the plaintiff who gifted the same to plaintiff including other suit property in CS Khatian Nos. 140 and 141 through Registered Deed No. 5900/3889 dated 30-9-93 and 9-5-90. Thus the plaintiff became owner and possessor of 132 decimals of the suit property which she could not develop due to non-partition. Plaintiff asked defendant to make partition of the suit property because the defendants occupied more than their entitlement. But the defendants refused to make partition of the suit property. Thereafter, the plaintiff filed a suit for permanent injunction and a title suit for recovery of possession being Title Suit No. 19 of 1990 and 42 of 1992 which were dismissed against which the plaintiff preferred an appeal but the appeal was also dismissed. Hence, the plaintiff filed the instant partition suit. 

 4. The defendants contested the suit by filing the written statements and admitted the plaintiff's title over 8 decimals of the suit land. The defendant further denied the material allegation made by the plaintiff in the plaint and stated that defendant was the owner and possessor of the suit property accepting 8 decimal of the suit land b virtue of Patta dated 5-6-47 issued by Nayeb of Zaminder in favour of Khodeja Akhter and Deel Bahar whose name was recorded in SA Khatian and who subsequently on 29-3-74 sold 16 decimal of 1 and to defendant No.5, 11 decimals of land to defendant No.6, 15 decimals ofland to defendant No.9, 17 decimals ofland to defendant No. 21 and 44 decimals of land to one Shamsuddin, Naimuddin Tejimuddin and Md Hanif who on 15-3-84 sold the property to defendant Nos. 1-4 and thus the defendants became owner and possessor of the suit land and the plaintiff had no right and title over the suit property excepting 8 decimal of land. The defendant further stated in his written statement that the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 19 of 1990 and 42 of 1992 which were dismissed and the appeals were also dismissed. 

 2. Whether the plaintiff has got any right title and possession over the suit land? 

 4. Whether the plaintiff is entitled to get preliminary decree in partition suit. 

 7. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 21-11-99 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Monohardi, Narsingdi in Title Suit No. 46 of 1996, the plaintiff preferred an appeal before the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narsingdi being Title Appeal No. 43 of 2000 stating, inter alia, that the  learned Senior Assistant Judge, Narsingdi did not apply his judicial mind and failed to consider and discuss the evidence on record properly. The learned Joint District Judge also without going through the merit of the suit and discussing the evidence on record and without considering the registered deed erroneously supported the decision and finding of the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Narsingdi and illegally dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court by his judgment and decree dated 13-11-2001. 

 9. The learned Advocate Mr Mushfiquddin Bakhtiar, appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the plaintiff successfully proved the case by adducing 4 witnesses and produced the registered deed executed by Manik Kishore on 3-12-88 in support of his right and title at least with regard to 32 decimals of the suit land. He further submits that the learned trial Court as well as the lower appellate Court without considering the registered deed and also the oral evidence of the witnesses partly decreed the suit. He further submits that the defendant on the basis of the Patta claimed his right and title over the suit land. But the Patta procured by the defendant appeared to be forged. 

 10. The learned Advocate Mr Md Manirul Islam Khan appearing on behalf of the defendant-respondent-opposite parties submits that the plaintiff prior to filing the partition suit filed a title suit being Title Suit No. 42 of 1991 which was dismissed then an appeal was preferred by the plaintiff being Title Appeal No. 17 of 1992 which was dismissed. Thereafter, the plaintiff filed another suit for permanent injunction being No. 19 of 1993 which was also dismissed. Thereafter, the instant partition suit been filed, as such, the partition suit is barred by res judicata. Next she submits that the defendant inherited the property from Khodeja Akhter and Deel Bahar who received the Patta from the Nayeb of Zaminder Suresh Chandra Singh on 5-6-1947 and since then they had been in peaceful possession of the suit land. He further submits that the defendant examined as many as 5 witnesses who categorically stated in their deposition about the right, title and possession of the suit land by the defendant. DW 1 Mojibur Rahman stated in his deposition that as a matter of fact the plaintiff has got no right, title and possession in the suit land and the original Patta was produced and exhibited by him as Exhibit-Gha. In this connection, the learned Advocate cited the decision in the case of Raja Sreenath Roy and others vs Moharaja Pratap Udai Nath Sahai Deo reported in Indian Cases Volume No. 82 Privy Council at page 879 wherein it was held- 

 "A Kabuliyat predicates a Patta. A Patta is granted by the Zaminder as a title deed to the tenant. The Kabuliyat, as its name implies, is a mere acknowledgment, an engagement by the tenant, to carry out the terms Of the Patta." 

 11. Next, he submits that the schedule of the suit land is vague and indefinite, as such, the plaintiff is not entitled to get any decree. He further submits that both the Courts below observed that the registered deed produced by the plaintiff is a faulty one. The caste of the vendor was written Muslim instead of Hindu and the district also wrongly written as Mohanganj instead of Mymensingh. Finally, he submits that the deed produced by the plaintiff is not genuine and he could not produce the original deed and on the basis of this sort of faulty deed the plaintiff cannot claim of the suit land for partition. Moreover, the plaintiff could not prove his right and title on the basis of this faulty document in the Title Suit No. 42 of 1991 and in the injunction suit No. 19 of 1993. The plaintiff miserably failed to prove the partition suit and, as such, the revisional application should be dismissed. 

 12. On a meticulous examination of evidence on record, registered deed, the judgments of both the Courts and other connected papers it appears that the learned trial Court by his judgment discussed the evidence and also the registered deed produced by plaintiff and observed that the plaintiff could not produce the original deed and the certified copy which was produced by the plaintiff appeared to be not genuine. The learned trial Court further observed that the partition suit is barred by res judicata but since defendant admitted that the 8 decimal of land is under the possession of the plaintiff and plaintiff has got title over the 8 decimal of land where his homestead is situated. The lower Appellate Court by his judgment and finding stated that the plaintiff could not prove his title and possession for 1.32 decimals of land in the title suit and also in the appeal arising out of the title suit. Thereafter, the lower appellate Court stated in his judgment that the plaintiff filed a suit for permanent injunction which Was also dismissed as because the plaintiff could not prove his possession by adducing any evidence. The learned lower appellate Court further observed that the registered documents which were produced by the plaintiff did not appear to prove right and title of the plaintiff. The lower appellate Court also observed that the Partition suit is barred by res judicata since the defendant admitted that the plaintiffs claim over 8 decimal of suit land arid right and title of plaintiff over the 8 decimal of land, the plaintiff is entitled to get 8 decimal of larid as his saham. The Court's below further observed that the suit land is vague and indefinite, as such, the suit of the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed.
